How to choose your application?

1. Does the app solve A specific problem?

Wrong choice: Install 10 apps “just in case”
Good choice: Identify your #1 problem (e.g. “I don't know what to sell” → install Copyfy | “I lose 70% of my visitors looking for a product” → install Algolia)

2. Is the app compatible with your theme?

Some AI apps break the design of your store. Always check:

  • Recent reviews (last 6 months)
  • Comments on popular themes (Dawn, Impulse, Prestige)
  • Responsive technical support

3. Does the app work well in French?

90% of AI apps are first developed in English. Verify:

  • Admin interface in French
  • AI trained on French (not just translated)
  • French speaking customer support

4. What is the impact on site speed?

AI apps can slow your site down by 0.5 to 2 seconds if poorly optimized.

Golden rule: Test your speed before and after installation with PageSpeed Insights

Lightweight apps: Copyfy (generates clean code), Shopify Magic (0 impact), SearchPie SEO, Boost AI
Heavy apps: Fast Simon, Algolia (but they compensate by converting)

5. What is the real level of automation?

Beware of bullshit marketing. Some “AI” apps require 10 hours of manual configuration.

Questions to ask:

  • Does the AI work from the moment it is installed? (ex: Copyfy = yes, store generated in 5 min | Fast Simon = no, 2-3h configuration)
  • Do I have to train the AI myself? (Gorgias = yes for 1 week)
  • How many hours of configuration? (indicated in the reviews)

What do you call a “winning product?”

A product research tool reduces uncertainty by combining signals. Only a measured test with a suitable offer, page and creatives validates potential for your store.

The 5 criteria for a winning product

Gross margin of at least x4/x5 the cost : If your product costs €5 to source (product + shipping + taxes), you must be able to sell it at least €25. This rule is non-negotiable. Common mistakes when looking for winning products

90% of newbies make these 7 mistakes that cost them time and money. Avoid them and you will already be in front of 90% of the competition.

Mistake 1: Believing in the miracle product

The best products are the ones that already work for others, not new innovations. Your differentiation = marketing angle, not the product itself.

The trap : Look for THE unique product that no one sells yet, think that you are going to revolutionize the market.

The reality : If no one is selling this product, it is because there is no market or because others have already tested and abandoned it. Successful entrepreneurs intelligently copy what works.

A product research tool reduces uncertainty by combining signals. Only a measured test with a suitable offer, page and creatives validates potential for your store.

Mistake 2: Starting a saturated trend

If 20+ stores sell exactly the same thing at the same angle, you're too late. Advertising costs are exploding (CPM at 15-20€ instead of 5-8€).

The trap : See a product in 50 stores and say to yourself “it works, I'm going to do it too”.

The reality : Competition is fierce, margins are squashed, and only first-movers make money. You're going to burn your budget with no results.

What to do : Look for products with 3-5 active competitors (sweet spot), or find a radically different angle if you want to go to a saturated market (example: massage roller for gamers instead of athletes).

Mistake 3: Neglecting the real margin

Most only calculate “sales price - product cost” and forget about hidden costs. As a result, they lose money on every sale.

The trap : Calculate only sales price - product cost, think that you can scale with an x3 margin.

Calculate real margin after product, shipping, taxes, fees, returns and acquisition. The viable multiplier depends on these unit economics.

What to do : Apply the minimum x5 rule. Product at 6€ all inclusive = sale at 30€. You have a margin of €24. You can spend €18 on advertising and keep €6 in net profit. Below x5, you go into the wall.

Mistake 4: Ignoring logistics

A product that arrives broken = refund + 1 star review + destroyed reputation. Bad reviews follow you for months.

The trap : Choose a fragile, bulky product or with a delay of 30 days to save €2.

The reality : A product that takes 4 weeks = unhappy customers + complaints + refunds. Saving €2 on the product costs you €50 in after-sales service.

What to do : Prefer light products (less than 500g), non-fragile, and with a maximum delay of 7-14 days. Or use an agent/warehouse in Europe to deliver in 3-5 days (cost +3-4 € but maximum customer satisfaction).

Mistake 5: Copying without a marketing angle

Using the same photos/videos/ads as a competitor = you will always be worse than him. It is 6 months in advance, thousands of reviews, and a huge advertising budget.

The trap : Take over exactly the same store, the same photos, the same ads as a successful competitor.

The reality : The competitor has already optimized its Facebook pixel, it has thousands of 5-star reviews, and it has a budget of €500/day. You can't win by copying exactly.

What to do : Same product, but different target (moms instead of everyone), different problem (anti-stress instead of organization), or different presentation (bundle 3 products instead of 1).

Mistake 6: Not testing fast enough

Spending 3 weeks fine-tuning the perfect store = procrastination in disguise. You'll never know if it's working until you launch.

The trap : Spend 3 weeks refining the design, descriptions, pages, before launching the first ad.

Name: 10 e-commerce product page examples that convert
Introduction: Your product pages aren't converting? Discover 10 e-commerce product page examples that turn a visitor into a customer, plus the template to copy.
Article:
In short:

  • An effective product page answers the visitor's questions right away and shows the benefits before the technical specs
  • An effective page brings together an optimised title, quality images, a compelling description, customer reviews and clear reassurance
  • The best pages use consumer psychology to turn a product's features into concrete benefits
  • SEO optimisation of a page relies on structured tags, technical data and solid internal linking
  • A checklist, a blank template and three ready-to-use templates to build high-performing pages in minutes

What do successful product page examples look like?

The market shows no mercy to a sloppy page. In France, according to Fevad:

  • more than 200,000 active e-commerce sites
  • around 42 million online shoppers
  • an average basket of about €65

In other words: dozens of stores already sell the same product as you, and it's the quality of the product page that tips the sale one way or the other.

We broke down 10 e-commerce product page examples that genuinely convert, from well-known big brands (Cabaïa, Décathlon, Lush, Gemmyo, Ledger, Lacoste, IKEA) to French dropshipping gems. For each one: what works, the strengths, the weak points and the lesson to apply to your own product page.

Example 1: Cabaïa, the product page that sells modularity

Product type: Accessory (modular backpack)
URL reviewed: https://www.cabaia.fr/products/sac-a-dos-adventurer-small-genoa

In the backpack market, everyone shows pretty much the same thing. The Cabaïa page stands out for one simple reason: it lets the customer build their bag instead of just presenting it to them.

What works:

  • The product choice is instantly readable: three sizes and many colourways can be picked without leaving the page
  • Modularity becomes a selling point: the front pocket swaps out, the bag is customised to the customer's taste
  • The price, the four interest-free instalments and free delivery above a threshold are shown without fuss
  • The variants appear as clickable product thumbnails, not a dull drop-down menu

Strengths:

  • Personalisation (size, colour, pocket) turns the page into a light configurator that engages the visitor
  • The visual variants help the customer picture themselves with it and increase time spent on the page

Weak points:

  • On a recent product, the lack of visible reviews deprives the page of reassuring social proof
  • Piling on options can dilute the decision if the visual hierarchy isn't held together

The lesson: when your product comes in several variants, show them as clickable thumbnails rather than a drop-down menu. The customer who builds their product is already committing to the purchase.

Example 2: Décathlon, the technical product page used as a model

Product type: Quechua 2 Seconds camping tent
URL reviewed: https://www.decathlon.fr/p/tente-de-camping-instantanee-2-places-2-seconds-easy-fresh-and-black/308355/

Want an example of a technical page that still sells? Look at Décathlon. The brand holds both ends at once: the benefit that creates desire, and the hard number that reassures behind it.

What works:

  • Three benefits in customer language right at the top of the page: "effortless camping", "darkness on demand"
  • A one-word setup summary, "2 seconds", more telling than any spec
  • A complete technical sheet in an accordion: waterproofing in Schmerber, wind resistance, weight, sleeping area dimensions
  • A 4.7/5 rating from nearly 1,000 reviews and a 5-year repairability commitment

Strengths:

  • The technical specs are tucked into an accordion: visible for those who look for them, hidden for everyone else
  • Every figure is measurable and verifiable, which builds confidence on a technical purchase

Weak points:

  • The density of information can overwhelm a beginner buyer
  • No section is explicitly labelled "benefits", which slightly dilutes the sales pitch

The lesson: tuck your specs into an accordion or a table, but always open with the benefit. The technical data reassures, the benefit triggers the desire.

Example 3: Lush, sensory storytelling pushed to the extreme

Product type: Solid cosmetic (bath bomb)
URL reviewed: https://www.lush.com/fr/fr/p/shoot-for-the-stars-bath-bomb

At Lush, the page for a simple bath bomb reads like a mouth-watering recipe. Everything goes through the senses, and that's exactly what makes the price acceptable.

What works:

  • A description that speaks to the senses: "caramelised starry sky", cocoa butter, coconut cream
  • Brand values shown as selling points: vegan, handmade, packaging-free, not tested on animals
  • An accessible, clickable ingredient list that reinforces transparency

Strengths:

  • The sensory vocabulary creates mental projection before the purchase even happens
  • The values become a differentiation lever, not a legal notice

Weak points:

  • Social proof is weak, with an average rating and few reviews, and visible negative comments
  • The price doesn't appear clearly on the page and some reviews stay in English, which creates friction

The lesson: brilliant storytelling never replaces solid social proof and a readable price. Polish the emotion, but don't forget the fundamentals that reassure.

Example 4: Gemmyo, the premium reassurance that takes the stress out of an expensive purchase

Product type: Bespoke jewellery (diamond ring)
URL reviewed: https://www.gemmyo.com/bague-or-blanc-18-cts-diamant-lady.html

Selling a ring worth over a thousand euros online, with no try-on, is a real challenge. Gemmyo pulls it off by stacking guarantees until the purchase feels almost risk-free.

What works:

  • A full configurator: metal, stone, diamond quality, size and engraving, with a transparent impact on price
  • Massive reassurance: lifetime warranty, free returns and resizing, instalment payments, French craftsmanship
  • Precise jewellery specs and an independent certificate that lend credibility to the value
  • The "word from the creative director" that adds a layer of emotion to the technical register

Strengths:

  • The stack of guarantees cancels out the perceived risk of a high-value purchase made remotely
  • The configurator turns the page into a personalised, educational experience

Weak points:

  • No rating or customer review on the page, even though trust is decisive at this price
  • The price hidden behind a "show price" button adds needless friction

The lesson: the higher the basket, the more visible and concrete the reassurance must be. But even a premium brand should never hide its reviews or its price.

Example 5: Ledger, the technical product page that sells peace of mind

Product type: Physical crypto wallet
URL reviewed: https://shop.ledger.com/products/ledger-nano-x

Ledger sells a technical object to an audience that isn't always technical. Its product page translates security, an abstract notion, into concrete benefits and certification proof.

What works:

  • A promise centred on the emotional benefit: take back control, "you alone approve"
  • Tangible security proof, such as a certified chip and a trusted screen, to back up the promise
  • A 4.4/5 rating from over 11,000 reviews and stated compatibility with thousands of cryptos
  • A "what's in the box" section and bundles that nudge toward a grouped basket

Strengths:

  • The box-contents section removes the uncertainty inherent to buying a technical product online
  • The comparison table between models helps the customer choose without leaving the page

Weak points:

  • The comparison itself admits a product limitation, a small screen and a multi-step journey
  • Delivery and warranty information stays barely visible on the page

The lesson: for a technical product, show what's in the box and compare your versions right there. You answer the two questions that block the purchase: "what do I get?" and "which one should I pick?".

Example 6: Lacoste, brand heritage as a selling point

Product type: Fashion (iconic polo)
URL reviewed: https://www.lacoste.com/fr/lacoste/homme/vetements/polos/manches-courtes/L1212-00.html

The L.12.12 polo has existed since 1933, and the page never lets you forget it. It's that brand story that justifies buying here rather than a copy at half the price.

What works:

  • Unapologetic storytelling ("the first polo ever invented", craftsmanship claimed out loud) that justifies the positioning
  • Precise features set against the history: piqué knit, weight, cut, mother-of-pearl buttons
  • A very high review volume, more than 3,500, that reassures on a purchase made without a try-on
  • Clear reassurance: free delivery and returns, size guide, personalisation

Strengths:

  • The brand narrative creates a perceived value that generic competitors cannot copy
  • The tabs (composition, cut, care, traceability) keep the page airy

Weak points:

  • The average rating doesn't show next to the review count, so part of the proof is lost
  • The tabs load in JavaScript and stay empty on first render: a risk for SEO and speed

The lesson: your brand story is an argument no one can duplicate. Tell it, but make sure your technical information stays readable by Google, not just by the browser.

Example 7: IKEA, the product page built for picturing it in your space

Product type: Furniture (modular bookcase)
URL reviewed: https://www.ikea.com/fr/fr/p/billy-bibliotheque-blanc-90522043/

For a piece of furniture, the customer's first fear is simple: "will it fit in my home?". IKEA builds its entire product page around that question.

What works:

  • Dimensions shown right in the title (width, depth, height) to answer the fear of clutter straight away
  • Modularity put forward: the unit completes with matching elements
  • In-context photos that help you picture it in your own home
  • Materials and an assembly guide clearly stated

Strengths:

  • The most decisive data, the dimensions, is also the most visible
  • The in-context projection turns an ordinary shelf into a storage solution

Weak points:

  • The shallow depth isn't put into perspective with its uses, for example large-format books
  • The entry-level positioning of the materials is barely framed as a benefit

The lesson: identify THE question that blocks the purchase of your product, then place the answer above the fold. For furniture it's the dimensions; for your product, it'll be something else.

Example 8: Digifeel, a B2B product with a guaranteed offer

Product type: Google Review Plaque (NFC solution for businesses)
URL: https://digifeel.fr/products/plaques-avis-google

This B2B page converts for one simple reason: it wipes out the risk from the title onward, with a promise that lands.

What works here:

  • The title gets straight to the point: "Google Review Plaque" with no frills, optimised for organic search
  • The hook defuses the number-one objection: "Double your number of Google reviews in 30 days or we refund you!". Hard to stay sceptical after that
  • Social proof shows from the start: 4.8/5 with 700+ verified reviews, at the top of the page
  • The benefits are listed as scannable bullet points:
    • "French Company" (location reassurance)
    • "Collect Reviews in 3 Seconds!" (speed benefit)
    • "One-off payment, 0 monthly fees" (pricing transparency)
    • "Be 1st in Google searches" (end result)
  • The packaged offers encourage a higher average basket:
    • 1-plaque pack: €29.90 (struck-through price €49.90)
    • 2-plaque pack: -40% + Free Guide
    • 5-plaque pack: -60% + Guide + Mystery Gift with a "Most popular" badge
  • The visuals are clear: a photo of the real product (NFC plaque) with an image gallery showing different angles and use contexts

Why it works:

The page knows its audience inside out. Shop owners and restaurateurs get stuck on two things: the price, and the doubt about whether it works. The 30-day money-back guarantee settles both in one go. And the discounts that climb with quantity push toward bulk buying, ideal for anyone running several outlets.

Standout strength: The "Save 60%" badge on the 5-plaque pack creates urgency and frames the premium offer as the smart move for anyone who wants to sell more.

Strengths:

  • The 30-day result guarantee removes the main objection of a B2B purchase
  • The tiered packs with gifts mechanically push the average basket upward

Weak points:

  • As the brand is little known, all the reassurance rests on the page itself
  • The lack of a demo video leaves part of the picture to the visitor's imagination

    How do you create an effective product page?

    Creating a product page is a conversation with your customer. You pin down what they're really looking for, and you answer without keeping them waiting.

    A product page doesn't just describe: it convinces, it converts, and it ranks on Google. Many online sellers pile up features. Except a list of specs sells nothing.

    What separates a page that informs from a page that sells? Buyer psychology, plain and simple. Your visitor doesn't want to know that your t-shirt is 80% cotton and 20% polyester. They want to know it'll be comfortable all day, that it won't lose its shape in the wash and that it'll give them a laid-back style perfect for the weekend.

    The golden rule: always present the benefits before the features. The technical features matter, but they come afterward to justify and lend credibility to your promises.

    Visitor's goalProduct page elementImpact on conversion
    Quickly understand the productClear title + main imageCaptures attention in 3 seconds
    Know whether it meets their needBenefit-oriented descriptionCreates mental projection
    Check the product's qualityCustomer reviews + real photosProvides social proof
    Eliminate the risksGuarantees + return policyLifts the final barriers to purchase

    An effective product page follows a precise structure: it starts by grabbing attention with a striking title and image visible without scrolling, it convinces with a benefit-focused description, it reassures with social proof and it makes action easy with an effective call to action.

    To build this structure, think about your own online buying behaviour. When you land on a web page, you rarely scroll all the way down before deciding. You scan quickly to find the information that matters. That's exactly what your visitors do.

    What are the elements of a product page?

    A complete product page assembles several blocks that, together, turn your visitor into a buyer. Each one has its function in the conversion, and each one lends a bit more credibility to your offer.

    SEO-optimised product title

    Your title must be clear, descriptive and contain the keywords your customers use to search for your product online. Avoid creative titles that say nothing about the actual product.

    Bad example: "The Summer Star"
    Good example: "Lightweight white linen summer dress, Flowing cut, Size S to XL"

    The good title includes the product type, the main feature and a practical detail such as the size or colour available.

    Product images

    The visual elements of a product page are the most viewed. You need several angles: a main photo on a white background, in-use photos, zooms on important details and ideally high-resolution images worn by real customers.

    Your visuals should show the product from every useful angle. A garment? Front, back, side, worn. An electronic accessory? The ports, the screen, the product in hand. Photo quality weighs heavily at the moment of deciding.

    Product description

    Your detailed description should have two parts, according to product page best practices:

    A short description that gets straight to the point with 2 to 3 punchy sentences on the main benefits. This part often appears at the top of the page and in search results.

    A long description that develops all the advantages, explains the use cases and answers common questions. Here, you can go deeper and give context to drive the purchase.

    Technical specifications

    List the specs clearly and easy to scan. Use bullets or a table so your visitor finds the information they're looking for in a few seconds.

    • Dimensions: 45 x 30 x 15 cm
    • Weight: 1.2 kg
    • Material: Water-resistant canvas
    • Capacity: 20 litres
    • Available colours: Black, Grey, Navy blue

    Price and promotions

    Show the product price clearly and highlight promotions if you offer any. If you offer a discount, show the old price struck through and the new price in large type to create a sense of urgency. This clear presentation builds trust and makes navigating your commercial offer easier. Be careful: urgency only works when it's real (genuine stock, genuine promos), because permanent fake countdowns and fake reference prices are counterproductive and risky.

    Customer reviews and social proof

    Customer reviews carry a lot of weight at the moment of deciding. Show the number of reviews, the average rating, and if possible a few detailed comments with photos. Seeing other buyers validate it reassures newcomers.

    Social proof works because it dissolves doubt: 500 buyers, 4.8 stars, the product surely holds up. Your social media can reinforce it all with genuine testimonials.

    Reassurance elements

    Reassure your visitor with clear information on:

    • Delivery (timeframes, costs, express options)
    • The return policy (how many days, free or not)
    • The warranty (duration, what it covers)
    • Secure payment (security badges, card accepted)
    • The customer service available to answer questions

    CTA (call to action)

    Your "Add to cart" button must be visible, contrasting and use a clear action verb. "Add to cart" works well, but you can also test "I want it" or "Order now" depending on your target audience.

    Optimised title Attract + rank High
    Quality images Show the product Very high

    Specifications Inform and add credibility Medium
    Clear price Make the decision easier High
    Customer reviews Reassure through social proof Very high

    How do you write a product page?

    Writing a product page well comes down to translating technical specs into concrete benefits. The AIDA method (Attention, Interest, Desire, Action) remains a solid framework for structuring your copy.

    Start by capturing Attention with a title and a first sentence that hit the mark. Your visitor must understand in 3 seconds what you're selling and why it matters to them.

    Build Interest by developing the main benefits. Don't just say your backpack has padded straps, explain that it lets you carry 10kg all day without back pain.

    Create Desire by helping your customer picture themselves using the product. Use phrases that start with "Imagine..." or "You'll be able to..." to create that mental projection.

    Prompt Action with a clear CTA and reassurance elements that lift the final barriers.

    Turning features into benefits

    This is the king skill in e-commerce copywriting. In front of each spec, ask yourself: "So what, what does that change for my customer?"

    Examples of features → benefits transformation:

    Feature: "5000 mAh battery"
    Benefit: "Lasts 3 full days without recharging, even with heavy use"

    Feature: "GOTS-certified organic cotton fabric"
    Benefit: "Soft on your skin and kind to the environment, perfect if you have sensitive skin"

    Feature: "Insulated bag with 8h insulation"
    Benefit: "Your meal stays fresh from morning to lunch, even in hot weather"

    Feature: "Non-slip rubber sole"
    Benefit: "Walk safely on wet floors without risking a slip"

    Adapting your tone to the product and the audience

    A technical product for professionals isn't written like a fashion accessory for young adults. Adapt your vocabulary and level of detail to your target audience based on your marketing positioning.

    For a beginner or general audience:

    • Use simple, accessible vocabulary
    • Explain technical terms if you have to use them
    • Favour everyday comparisons ("As light as a water bottle")
    • Adopt a friendly, reassuring tone

    For an expert or professional audience:

    • Use the appropriate technical vocabulary
    • Give precise and complete specs
    • Compare with market standards
    • Stay professional while remaining accessible

    Fill-in-the-blank product page template to start quickly:

    [PRODUCT TITLE], [MAIN BENEFIT], [PRACTICAL INFO]

    [BENEFIT HOOK in 1-2 sentences]

    Why you'll love it:
    - [Benefit 1]
    - [Benefit 2]
    - [Benefit 3]

    [EXPANDED DESCRIPTION with projection into use]

    Specifications:
    - [Spec 1] = [What it gives you]
    - [Spec 2] = [What it gives you]
    - [Spec 3] = [What it gives you]

    [REASSURANCE SECTION: Delivery, Return, Warranty]

    [CLEAR CTA]

    Examples of before / after optimisation sentences

    Before: "This product is made with high-quality materials."
    After: "Made from aerospace-grade aluminium, this product resists shocks and daily wear for years."

    Before: "Our t-shirt is available in several sizes."
    After: "Find your perfect size among 7 options, from XS to XXL, with our detailed size guide."

    Before: "This headset has good battery life."
    After: "Listen to your music for 30 hours without interruption, that's 2 weeks of use for a daily 1h commute."

    The key to good product page writing is to speak to your customer as if you were in store standing in front of them. What would you say to convince them? What questions would they ask you? Answer those questions in your page to sell effectively.

    • Break your text into short blocks with clear subheadings
    • Bold the important words to guide the eye
    • Leave white space to give your page room to breathe
    • Take care with your font choice for comfortable reading

    A simple test: if you blur your product page and you can no longer identify the important blocks of information, then your visual hierarchy isn't clear enough.

    Visual hierarchy and information organisation

    Organise the information from most important to least important. The inverted pyramid applies at full force here, and your visitor finds what they're looking for faster.

    Recommended structure from top to bottom:

    1. Title + Price + Review rating
    2. Main images + CTA
    3. Short description (main benefits)
    4. Visible reassurance elements
    5. Expanded long description
    6. Technical specifications
    7. Detailed customer reviews
    8. Complementary products or cross-sell

    The most important information (what it is, how much it costs, whether it's well rated) must be visible without scrolling, ideally positioned on the left for natural Western reading.

    Mobile first: optimising for the smartphone screen

    The majority of e-commerce traffic now comes from mobile. Your page is therefore designed for the smartphone first, the computer second. Load speed and mobile comfort weigh heavily on your conversion rate.

    Mobile best practices:

    • Show the price and the CTA sticky at the bottom of the screen
    • Use accordions for long sections: description, specifications, FAQ
    • Optimise your images for fast loading
    • Make the buttons big enough to tap with a finger (minimum 44x44 pixels)
    • Place the critical information within the first 2 screens
    • Ensure smooth navigation between sections

    On mobile, every second of loading counts. If your page takes more than 3 seconds to display, you're already losing potential customers.

    Brand consistency and visual identity

    Your page should carry your brand identity without sacrificing effectiveness. Button colour, copy tone, photo style: everything matches the image you want to project, in line with your brand guidelines.

    A young, offbeat brand will use a friendly tone, emojis, bright colours and relaxed lifestyle photos. A premium, minimalist brand will prefer a calmer tone, generous white space and clean photos on a neutral background.

    Do / don't list for a high-performing product page:

    Do:

    • Start with the benefits before the features
    • Use several quality photos from different angles
    • Include customer reviews with photos if possible
    • Clearly show delivery and return info
    • Test different versions of your CTA
    • Optimise for mobile as a priority
    • Add videos of the product in action when relevant
    • Include a size guide or clear dimensions
    • Offer personalisation options when possible
    • Add relevant cross-sell suggestions

    Don't:

    • Drown the important information in walls of text
    • Use only white-background photos with no context
    • Copy-paste supplier descriptions
    • Hide shipping costs until the end of the checkout funnel
    • Use technical jargon without explaining it
    • Put 10 different CTAs that create confusion
    • Forget to optimise the images (weight and ALT)
    • Offer too many options that paralyse the decision
    • Neglect the experience on a small mobile screen

    A concrete example of improvement:

    You sell a LED desk lamp. Instead of saying "15W LED lamp with 3 brightness levels", write "Adapt the brightness to your activity: intense reading, screen work or soft ambient lighting". The customer instantly understands how they'll use the 3 levels.

    Testing and improving continuously

    The best pages are never set in stone: they move to the rhythm of feedback and data, through A/B tests. Test several versions of your key elements and watch the conversion rate react in real time.

    Elements to A/B test:

    • The title and the short description
    • The colour and text of the CTA
    • The order of the information
    • The type of visuals (lifestyle vs packshot)
    • Whether or not there's a video
    • The price positioning (top right vs left)

    Also look at the questions your customers ask you by email or in reviews. If several people ask the same question, it's a sign that this information should be more visible in your page. You can even add a FAQ section at the bottom of the page to anticipate those queries.

    How do you optimise a product page for SEO?

    Optimising a page's SEO means making your product appear on Google exactly when someone searches for what you sell. Free, qualified traffic, straight to your page. Applied well, these techniques can multiply your visibility.

    Optimised title and meta description

    Your title tag (the title that appears in Google's results) must contain your main keyword and make people want to click. You have around 60 characters to convince.

    Structure of a good title tag:
    [Main keyword], [Differentiating element] | [Brand name]

    Example: "Waterproof 30L backpack, 5-year warranty, [Your Brand]"

    Your meta description (the text below the title in Google) must summarise the main benefits in 155 characters maximum. Include a call to action and the elements that set you apart according to your content strategy.

    Example: "Protect your gear in all weather. 100% waterproof, ultra-tough 30L backpack. Free delivery and 60-day returns. 5-year warranty included."

    Hn structure: heading hierarchy

    A clean heading structure helps Google read your content's organisation, and makes the page nicer to browse. A genuine pillar of organic search.

    Typical structure:

    • H1: Main product title (only 1 per page)
    • H2: Main sections (Description, Specifications, Reviews)
    • H3: Sub-sections if needed

    Your H1 must be unique, descriptive and contain your main keyword. For example: "Breathable men's running shoes, Trail Pro model"

    Image ALT tags for accessibility and search

    Each image on your product page must have a descriptive ALT attribute. It matters for accessibility (screen readers for the visually impaired) and for improving the ranking of your visuals on Google Images.

    Bad ALT: "IMG_2847.jpg"
    Good ALT: "Black men's running shoes worn on a forest trail"

    Describe precisely what's visible in the image while naturally including your relevant keywords. Avoid keyword stuffing, stay natural and descriptive.

    Product structured data (schema.org)

    Structured data lets Google display rich information in its results: price, availability, review rating. Enough to boost your click-through rate and your visibility.

    The essential Product data to implement:

    • Product name
    • Image
    • Description
    • Price and currency
    • Availability (in stock / out of stock)
    • Average rating and number of reviews
    • SKU or product reference

    Most e-commerce platforms (Shopify, WooCommerce, PrestaShop) automatically include this structured data. Check anyway with Google's rich results test tool to make sure everything works correctly.

    Managing duplicate content: a crucial issue

    Duplicate content is the number-1 problem in e-commerce organic search. If you copy supplier descriptions or if you have several variants of the same product, Google can penalise you and lower your chance of appearing on the first page.

    Solutions against duplicate content:

    • Write your own descriptions, never copy-paste from the supplier
    • Use the canonical tag for variants (the same product in different colours)
    • Create unique descriptions even for similar products
    • Add unique content: customer reviews, FAQ, usage guides

    If you have 50 different t-shirts, don't copy the same description just changing the colour. Vary the benefits put forward, the use examples, the tone.

    Strategic internal linking

    Internal linking means connecting your pages to each other, to help Google explore your site and send your visitors toward other relevant products. A double bonus: your ranking improves, and so does your average basket.

    Effective internal linking strategies:

    • Links from your category to your flagship products
    • A "Similar products" or "You may also like" section
    • Contextual links in your descriptions ("Perfect with our laptop sleeve")
    • Buying guides that point to specific products
    • Bundles or packs that group several products together

    Good internal linking helps your visitor discover more products and improves your ranking by distributing the "SEO juice" across your whole website.

    SEO checklist for a product page:

    • [ ] Unique title tag with main keyword (max 60 characters)
    • [ ] Compelling meta description (max 155 characters)
    • [ ] Unique, descriptive H1 on each page
    • [ ] Logical Hn structure (H2 for sections, H3 for sub-sections)

    • [ ] Internal linking to complementary products
    • [ ] Load time < 3 seconds

    Example of an SEO-optimised product page:

    Let's imagine a page for bluetooth sport earphones.

    URL: /bluetooth-sport-earphones-waterproof-running
    Title: Bluetooth Sport Earphones IPX7, Perfect running fit | [Brand]
    H1: Waterproof IPX7 bluetooth sport earphones, Perfect for running and fitness

    The page targets the keyword "bluetooth sport earphones" and slips in variants like "running" and "waterproof" along the way. From the very first lines, it answers the search intent: finding earphones that don't move during exercise.

    FAQ: everything to know about the product page

    What is a product page?

    A product page is the page of an online store that presents an item for sale. It brings together the title, the images, the price, the description, the specifications, the customer reviews and the buy button. Its role: give the visitor all the information to decide, then convert them into a buyer.

    How do you make a product page?

    To create an effective product page, start with a clear title, add quality images, write a benefit-oriented description, list the specifications, show the price and the reviews, then finish with a visible call to action. Always present the benefits before the technical features.

    What are the elements of a product page?

    A successful product page has twelve elements: title, image gallery, price, rating and reviews, hook, benefits, long description, technical specifications, reassurance, social proof, call to action and cross-sell. Each one plays a precise role in converting the visitor into a customer.

    How do you write an e-commerce product description?

    Write a product description by turning each feature into a concrete benefit for the customer. Use the AIDA method, attention, interest, desire, action, vocabulary suited to your audience and short sentences. A short description highlights the benefits, a long description develops the uses.

    How do you optimise a product page for SEO?

    Optimise your product page with a title tag and a meta description containing your main keyword, a logical heading structure, descriptive ALT tags on the images and Product structured data. Write unique content to avoid duplicate content and take care with your internal linking.

    What is a Shopify product page?

    A Shopify product page is the product page generated by the Shopify platform. It's managed from the admin with a title, an HTML description, media, a price and variants. Apps let you add reviews, accordions and reassurance to make it more convincing.

    How do you use these templates?

    These templates are starting points, to shape according to your product and your brand. Adjust the tone, shorten or lengthen the sections depending on the complexity, and test several versions to see which one converts best.

    The key is to keep your focus on the benefits for your customer instead of getting lost in the purely technical description. Even a very specialised product talks benefit first, specs second. Keep that reflex for all your content creation.

Do you spend a lot of money on Facebook Ads without knowing if your advertising campaigns are well structured? This guide covers the testing method, scaling, the creatives who convert, and calculating your true profitability in dropshipping advertising. You leave with a campaign structure applicable today and the numerical guidelines to manage your ads.

Before launching your first ad: the prerequisites

Launching an ad on Facebook without preparation is a drain on the budget. You need to have three things in place on your website before spending a single euro to promote your dropshipping store.

The Facebook pixel and the Conversions API

The Facebook pixel is a piece of code installed on your dropshipping store that tracks the actions of your users: addition to the basket, start of payment, purchase. Without it, the algorithm works blindly.

Combine the available tracking tools and check event quality. Data loss varies with the setup.

Also remember to configure the domain check in your Facebook Ads Manager. Many forget it, and it limits your targeting options and ad performance.

A product validated by the market

Before launching your ads, validate the request:

  • Verify that competitors are already spending on advertising on this product. Copyfy's adspy tool allows you to analyze Facebook Ads directly and identify winning products
  • Look at the traffic volume of shops selling a similar product
  • Order the product yourself to understand its strengths and weaknesses
  • Analyze customer reviews on Amazon and AliExpress to identify recurring objections

A clean Business Manager

Create a Business Manager account on business.facebook.com if you haven't already done so. Connect your Facebook page, Instagram, and ad account. Also add your store as a Facebook Shop so that your users can interact with your products directly on the social network.

A well-structured account from the start will prevent you from bans and restrictions later on. And believe me, recovering a blocked account is a nightmare.

How to structure your Facebook Ads campaigns

The era of complicated structures with 15 ad sets and 50 different interests is over. Meta's algorithm has evolved. He prefers simple structures that he can optimize freely. The Facebook advertising strategy, consists of two campaigns.

The 2-campaign structure

Testing campaign. This is where you test your creative concepts (hooks, angles, formats). The objective: to identify Facebook ads that generate clicks and purchases.

You launch several creatives in parallel with a small budget per ad set (5 to 15€ per day) and you let 3 to 5 days run to collect enough data.

Set test budget and duration from your maximum CPA, margin and the amount of data collected. No fixed amount or timeframe fits every product.

Raise budgets in steps while monitoring CPA, volume and margin. Test the size and pace of increases on the account.

There's no need for 5 campaigns with audiences segmented in every way. Simplicity wins.

Advantage+ Shopping Campaign: for or against?

Meta offers Advantage+ Shopping (ASC) campaigns that automate targeting and bidding using machine learning. It works well for established stores that already have conversion data.

For a beginner who is testing a new product, the manual campaign is still preferable. It gives you more control and allows you to understand what works. Switch to Advantage+ once your Pixel has accumulated enough data.

Targeting: why broad targeting dominates

Interest-based targeting has long been the norm in dropshipping. You selected interests like “yoga” or “tech gadgets” to reach your target audience.

Test broad, interests and lookalikes against account data. No option wins in every case.

Broad works on one condition: your creatives must be eloquent enough for the algorithm to understand who to show your ad to.

Concrete example. Does your video show a back massage product? Facebook will be able to find Internet users interested in relieving back pain. No need to tell him.

Create Facebook ads that convert

Targeting matters. But the creative makes all the difference. The algorithm manages targeting automatically better and better. What separates you from your competitors is the quality of your Facebook ads and visual content.

Formats that work

Test formats, hooks and angles suited to the product. Required volume and creative lifespan vary by market and budget. Further reading : Facebook Ads video formats.

Your video should show the product in action and solve a visible problem. No Hollywood production needed. A smartphone, good light, and a clear script are all you need.

UGC (User Generated Content). Videos from “real people” that show how they use your product work better than slick ads. Meta pushes this type of high-quality content because it generates more engagement.

The typical format: someone in front of the camera who presents a problem, shows the solution (your product) and shares their opinion. It inspires confidence because it doesn't look like a typical sponsored post.

The carousel. Well suited to show multiple angles of a product, different variants, or a before-and-after. Each image should have an eye-catching visual and a short description. Add a call to action such as “Swipe to see available colors.”

Dynamic ads (DPA). They automatically show visitors the products they have already viewed on your store. Connect your product catalog to Meta Commerce Manager to activate them.

The anatomy of a winning creative

Then you present your product as the answer. Show it in action. Add a piece of social proof (customer reviews, sales, testimonials) and finish with a clear call to action: “Order now” or “Take advantage of 30% off.”

This structure works just as well in video as in static images. The hook is still the most important part. If you don't get attention in the first 3 seconds, the rest has no impact.

Producing volume

Creative people have a limited lifespan. They run out of steam after a few weeks. Successful media buyers test 50 or more creatives per month.

Don't start from scratch every time. When a creative works well, decline it. Change the hook. Change the angle. Try a new format.

It's called creative iteration. You keep what converts and you refresh what tires you.

A good reflex: analyze the advertisements of your competitors via the facebook ads library or via an adspy tool like the one built into Copyfy. Ads that have been running for a long time are profitable, otherwise they would have been cut. Get inspired by the angle, format, and tone without copying.

What budget for a dropshipping Facebook ad

This is THE question everyone asks when they want to use Facebook Ads for their dropshipping business. The honest answer: it depends on your product and your margins.

The minimum viable

To seriously test a product, plan between 300 and 500€ from Facebook Ads Budget. This allows you to launch 3 to 5 different creatives with a daily budget of 5 to 15€ per ad set for 5 to 7 days.

This budget does not guarantee profitability. He gives you data. And data is what allows you to make decisions.

If you have a more comfortable Facebook budget (€1,000 to €5,000), you can test several products in parallel and iterate more quickly.

Successful entrepreneurs don't find a winning product the first time. They test 5, 10, sometimes 20 before finding the one that is a hit.

How to calculate your profitability

ROAS (Return On Ad Spend) is the most used metric to analyze Facebook Ads. An ROAS of 3 means that for every euro spent on advertising, you generate €3 in turnover.

But ROAS is misleading if you don't take all your costs into account:

Net profit = Sales price - (product cost + delivery costs + advertising costs + transaction fees)

An ROAS of 3 may seem fine. But if your margins are low and delivery is expensive, you can be at a loss despite a good ROAS.

Read CPM, CTR, CPC, conversion, CPA and ROAS together. Useful thresholds depend on the market, offer and unit economics.

By optimizing your creative skills and retargetting your visitors, this number increases over time.

Metric Benchmark What It Tells You

Conversion Rate > 2% on the landing page The quality of your product page
Cost Per Purchase Depends on your margin Your actual profitability
ROAS > 2 to be profitable Your return on ad spend

Don't look at these numbers after 24 hours in a panic. Give the algorithm 3 to 5 days to get out of the learning phase before drawing conclusions.

The step by step testing method

Testing intelligently is the core of dropshipping marketing. You can apply this method right now for your Facebook Ads.

Step 1: Get your creatives ready

Before touching the Business Manager, produce at least 3 to 5 different creatives for your product. Vary the angles:

  • “Problem/solution” angle: you show the pain and then the product as a remedy
  • “Demonstration” angle: you show the product in action without frills
  • “Testimonial” angle: a customer or influencer talks about their experience
  • “Comparison” angle: before and after or your product vs the competition

Step 2: Start your testing advertising campaign

Create a campaign in the Facebook Ads Manager with the objective sales. One ad set per creative, broad targeting (no interest, just the age group and the country).

Budget: 10 to 15€ per ad set per day.

Each ad set contains only one creative. Why? Because you want to isolate variables.

If you put 5 ads in the same ad set, Facebook will focus the budget on one and you won't have data on the others.

Step 3: analysis after 3 to 5 days

After 3 to 5 days, you have enough data to decide. Look at the cost per purchase for each creative.

  • Cost per profitable purchase : you keep the creative and you scale
  • High cost per purchase but good CTR : optimize your product page, not your ad
  • Low CTR (< 1%) : your creative doesn't catch on, test a new hook
  • No conversion after €500 : question the product itself

Step 4: Scale what works

Raise budgets in steps while monitoring CPA, volume and margin. Test the size and pace of increases on the account.

Sudden budget increases push the algorithm out of its optimization zone. Your costs are temporarily exploding and you are losing accumulated data.

At the same time, continue to test creative news in your testing campaign. A winning creative always ends up burning out. You need to have the next one ready.

Retargeting: turning visitors into buyers

Retargeting can complement cold acquisition. Measure its incremental impact and profitability instead of applying a universal multiplier.

Essential retargeting audiences

  • Website visitors (7 days): the hottest, they have just browsed your products
  • Add-ons to the cart without a purchase (14 days): a little push is often enough to trigger the order
  • Site visitors (30 to 180 days): large audience to maintain brand awareness
  • Social media commitments (Instagram/Facebook): those who liked, commented, or watched your videos

The message changes according to the audience

Do not show the same ad to someone who discovers you and to someone who has already put a product in their basket.

To retarget cart abandonments, use creative people who remove objections: money back guarantee, free delivery, positive customer reviews. A promo code can also change the decision.

For older visitors, recall the benefits of the product from a different perspective than the one that first brought them in.

Why does Facebook Ads still work for dropshipping?

Every year, we hear that Facebook Ads is dead for dropshipping. And every year, online retailers who master the platform continue to generate results.

Assess Facebook with current official data and, above all, your own account results; general averages do not predict profitability.

Facebook has an advantage that few social networks can match: data depth. When you advertise on Facebook, you're not just targeting people who like “fitness” or “decorating.”

You get access to an algorithm that analyzes billions of behavioral signals to find the users who are most likely to buy your product.

With Instagram, Messenger, and the Audience Network included in the placements, a single ad campaign touches a complete social ecosystem.

Facebook Ads or Google Ads: what should you choose for dropshipping?

Choosing between Google and Facebook is a common question. The two platforms serve different purposes. It's not an “or” choice but rather an “and” when you have the budget.

Criteria Facebook Ads Google Ads
Type of Demand Created demand (you show a product to someone who wasn't looking for it) Existing demand (the person is actively searching for a product)
Main Strength Behavioral targeting and eye-catching visuals High purchase intent (Search)
Ideal For Product testing, fast scaling, viral products Products with existing search volume
Starting Budget More affordable (€5-15/day per ad set) More expensive depending on keyword competition
Learning Curve Moderate More technical (Search, Shopping, Display)

Choose Meta, Google or TikTok according to intent, product, creative fit, market and available budget.

Google Ads also becomes relevant once you have validated your product and Internet users start looking for your brand or type of product directly on Google.

TikTok Ads also deserves a mention. The social network attracts a young audience and the costs are sometimes lower than Facebook. But the results are less predictable when you start out. Some e-commerce merchants also use Pinterest to develop organic dropshipping alongside paid advertising.

The mistakes that are expensive (and how to avoid them)

After hundreds of campaigns analyzed, the same errors come up again in advertising on Facebook.

Change ads after 24 hours. The algorithm needs time to optimize. Cut an ad too early and you lose the initial investment without usable data. Wait at least 3 days.

Neglect the product page. Your ad can be perfect. If your website is slow, poorly written, or without customer reviews, no one will buy. Advertising brings traffic. The page is converting. They are two different jobs.

Test broad, interests and lookalikes against account data. No option wins in every case.

Not testing enough creatives. If you only test 2 ads per month, you're moving at a slow pace. The best ones test dozens of variations. Ad creatives is the No. 1 lever.

Forget to look at the net profit. An ROAS of 4 is impressive. But if your margins are low, you can still lose money. Always calculate your real profit.

You have a profitable advertising campaign. How to scale your campaign from €50/day to €500/day without your costs exploding?

Increase the budget gradually

Raise budgets in steps while monitoring CPA, volume and margin. Test the size and pace of increases on the account.

Duplicate on secondary markets

If you sell in France with positive results, test Belgium, Switzerland and French-speaking Canada. These are smaller markets with less competition.

Advertising costs are often lower there.

For products without linguistic constraints (gadgets, accessories), also test the United Kingdom, Germany or the Netherlands with adapted ads.

If your winning creative is a 15-second video in the News Feed, create it in a 9:16 vertical format for Stories and Reels.

Meta is actively pushing Reels content on its social networks. You take advantage of the algorithm by playing the game.

Also test carousels and ads in collection format for retargeting audiences.

Add upsells and bundles

Scaling is not only done on the ad side. Increase your average basket by offering complementary products and bundles on your dropshipping store.

A higher average basket allows you to absorb a higher cost per purchase while remaining profitable on your dropshipping business.

What separates good media buyers from others

Facebook Ads in dropshipping is as much about marketing as it is about customer psychology. Entrepreneurs who last are those who understand their target audience better than their competitors.

Call your first customers. Ask them why they bought. Analyze abandoned carts to understand what is blocking the buying journey.

Read the reviews of your competitors on Amazon and AliExpress to identify recurring frustrations. Each feedback collected brings you closer to more relevant advertising and an offer that better answers the problem.

Limits, risks and mistakes to avoid

Let's be honest: AI dropshipping is not a magic bullet. There are real limits, risks to be aware of, and classic mistakes that can cost you dearly. But by knowing them in advance, you can easily avoid them.

AI is no substitute for understanding the market

These figures are estimates and signals, not proof of profit. Check the potential against your costs and your own tests.

The best entrepreneurs use AI as a co-pilot, not as an autopilot. They analyze, test quickly, adjust and refine their positioning. AI speeds up the whole process, but you keep control of the strategy.

Excessive dependence on tools

If you build your business entirely on AI tools without understanding the fundamentals, you are vulnerable. The day the tool changes its price, changes its functionalities, or closes, you find yourself stuck.

The right approach: use AI to go faster, but at the same time learn the basics of marketing, conversion, and analysis.

Major risks:

  • Fast saturation of trending products detected by AI
  • Variable quality of content generated without supervision
  • Dependence on applications whose algorithms you don't know
  • Over-optimization that makes sites too similar
  • Loss of human contact and authenticity

Monitor competing offers and your own acquisition costs. A product found by several sellers may face more competition without automatically losing its margin. Grow gradually only when margin, supplier and cash flow allow.

AI doesn't do everything by itself

Let's be clear: AI dropshipping is not passive. You still have to manage your advertising campaigns, analyze your results, solve complex customer problems, negotiate with suppliers, optimize your margins. AI automates repetitive tasks, strategic management remains in your hands.

Workload varies with orders, tools and incidents. Measure actual time spent on checks, ads and support: there is no universal weekly minimum or guaranteed autonomous store.

Classic mistakes

Wanting to automate before understanding. That is the mistake that almost everyone makes at the beginning. First you need to understand how dropshipping works, conversion mechanics, and how to analyze ads. Only then do you automate what you control. Otherwise you're just going to automate... mistakes.

Trust AI recommendations blindly. The algorithm may be wrong. A product may look perfect on paper but not match your audience. Always test on a small scale before scaling. It's less sexy than going straight for it, but it will save you a lot of money.

What to keep in mind:

  • AI is a powerful resource, not a complete strategy
  • Product quality and customer service remain essential
  • You need to maintain human control over important decisions
  • The best results come from the hybridization of AI + human expertise
  • It takes time to master the tools, but it comes quickly

AI dropshipping really works, but only if you use it smartly. Think of it as an enhancer of your skills, not as a replacement. The more you learn, the more powerful AI makes you.

Export settings that prevent Facebook from ruining your video

You can have the perfect dimensions, the perfect creative, the perfect hook. Then Facebook re-encodes your video and it comes out blurry.

This happens because Facebook compresses every single upload through its own encoding pipeline. You never serve your original file to viewers.

The trick: feed Facebook's encoder the highest-quality source possible. Here's your pre-upload checklist for proper video settings:

  • Container and codec: MP4 with H.264 video compression + AAC audio. Do not upload H.265 files. Facebook's encoder handles H.264 input more reliably.
  • Pixel format: square pixels, fixed frame rate, progressive scan. These settings ensure optimal compatibility across all devices.
  • Bitrate: 8 to 12 Mbps for 1080p. Going up to 15-20 Mbps is fine. Going lower than 8 Mbps is where blur starts after recompression.
  • Frame rate: 30 fps, constant frame rate (CFR). Facebook caps playback at 30 fps anyway. Uploading 60 fps doubles your file size for zero visible benefit.
  • Audio: Stereo AAC audio compression at 128 kbps minimum. Push to 192 kbps for dialogue or voiceover.
  • Encoding pass: Use 2-pass VBR if your software supports it. It allocates bitrate more efficiently across fast and static scenes.
  • Resolution: export at 1080p native (1080x1350 feed, 1080x1920 Stories/Reels). Shot in 4K? Still export 1080p. Exception: 1440x2560 for Reels on 20:9 Android.

Avoid double compression. This is the mistake that kills quality most often. If you re-export a previously compressed video, each generation stacks artifacts. Always export from your original project file.

5 mistakes that silently waste your ad budget

Uploading one video size for all placements. A single 1:1 square video looks fine in Feed but gets letterboxed in Stories and Reels. Your full-screen ad becomes a tiny square floating in black. Users scroll past instantly.

Ignoring safe zones on Reels. Your CTA at the bottom of the video? Invisible under the like button and caption overlay. Always preview in Ads Manager with the safe zone guardrail on before publishing.

Exporting at 720p to "save space." Facebook's 4 GB limit is generous. A 15-second 1080p video at 12 Mbps is roughly 22 MB. No reason to compress to 720p.

Leaving Advantage+ Creative on by default. Auto-crop, text overlay, and motion effects can work against professional creative. If you've designed assets for each placement, disable these enhancements.

Forgetting captions. A huge share of Facebook users watch with sound off. No captions means no message. Tools like CapCut generate auto-captions in seconds. No excuse to skip this today.

Not testing across devices before launch. Your ad might look perfect on a MacBook but get cropped on a Samsung Galaxy with a 20:9 screen. Meta handles this by using "Smart Zoom" (crops edges) or letterboxing. Always preview on at least one Android and one iPhone before going live.

FAQ

What are the recommended video ad specs for Facebook today?

For feed ads, use 1080 x 1350 pixels (4:5 ratio). For Facebook Stories and Facebook Reels, use 1080 x 1920 pixels (9:16). For Facebook carousel, go with 1080 x 1080 pixels (1:1). All placements require file type MP4 or MOV with H.264 compression, square pixels, fixed frame rate, progressive scan, and stereo AAC audio compression. Maximum file size is 4 GB.

What's the maximum file size for a Facebook video ad?

4 GB across all placements. In practice, most 15 to 60 second ads at 1080p are well under 100 MB with proper H.264 encoding. If your video file is approaching the limit, it likely means your bitrate is extremely high or your video duration is very long.

How long can a Facebook video ad be?

Video duration ranges from 1 second to 241 minutes for feed placements. But optimal length is 15 seconds or less for the news feed, under 10 seconds for Stories, and under 30 seconds for Reels. Attention spans on mobile are short. Say your piece fast.

What aspect ratio should I choose if I can only make one video?

Go with 1:1 (1080 x 1080 pixels). It displays cleanly across feed, Facebook carousel, and Facebook Marketplace without cropping. It won't fill the screen on Stories or Reels, but it's the most compatible single format. If you can make two versions, add a 9:16 for Stories and Reels.

Does Facebook accept MOV or GIF files?

Yes. Facebook supports MP4, MOV, and GIF file types for video ads. However, MP4 with H.264 compression tends to process faster and more reliably. GIF is supported but limited in quality and file size. Stick with MP4 for proper video ad campaigns.

Why does my video look blurry after uploading to Facebook?

Facebook re-encodes every video file. If your source was already heavily compressed or exported at a low bitrate, the re-encoding stacks compression artifacts. Export at 8 to 12 Mbps for 1080p, use H.264 (not H.265), and always compress from your original project file. Also check that you're uploading from a desktop browser or Meta Business Suite rather than the mobile app, which can apply additional compression.

Should I upload separate videos for each placement or use one universal video?

If you're serious about conversion performance, upload separate videos. A 4:5 for feed, a 9:16 for Facebook Stories and Reels, and a 1:1 for carousels. Then use Meta's Adapt to Placement feature to assign each version to its intended spot. This way you control exactly what the user sees instead of relying on automatic cropping. If you don't have the bandwidth for that, one 1:1 video is the safest single-format option.

Getting the video ad specs right is the foundation. But specs alone don't drive conversions.

You need creative that stops the scroll, a hook that grabs in under 3 seconds, and an offer that makes users act. Beware of the traps!

To avoid the pitfalls, you have to know them first.

The compliance trap. Amazon is closely monitoring the performance of sellers. Thresholds that should never be exceeded:

  • ODR (Order Defect Rate): under 1%
  • Pre-shipment cancellation rate: under 2.5%
  • Late shipping rate: under 4%

A failed supplier destroys these metrics in a few weeks. This is an outcome that you should absolutely avoid.

The trap of unsuitable suppliers. Using Chinese suppliers with deadlines of 15 to 30 days is a Bad idea on Amazon. The platform expects deliveries in less than 5 days. Sourcing should focus on local or European suppliers who are able to ship directly to the customer within these deadlines.

The dropshipping margin trap is too low. Amazon commissions range between 8 and 15% depending on the category. Add PPC advertising costs (often 10-15% of sales) and subscription fees. If your product does not generate a minimum gross margin of 30 to 40%, you are working at a loss. An experienced e-merchant aims for a coefficient of at least x4 between purchase price and sale price.

The trap of retail arbitration. Buy on a website Large-scale distribution for resale is prohibited. Only sourcing via authorized wholesalers or directly at the source is compliant. In response, Amazon is strengthening its controls every year.

Ce economic model works as long as you treat it like a real business. Many people on the internet present dropshipping as a magic formula. The reality is different.

Successful salespeople share three traits: products with solid margins from the start, reliable suppliers who can deliver quickly, and a constant investment in optimizing their listings and their customer service.

Introduction: Understand how dropshipping works, its costs and your responsibilities as a seller before launching your store.
Article:
Key takeaways:

  • The supplier ships to customers; you remain responsible for the sale and service.
  • The model limits initial inventory but retains financial risks.
  • Calculate profitability after acquisition, delivery, returns, fees and taxes.

Definition of dropshipping:

Dropshipping is a sales model without inventory to manage for customer orders: the supplier holds and ships products. You operate the store and remain responsible to the buyer.

You delegate storage and shipping to the supplier while managing the offer and customer relationship. You still need to inspect samples before selling.

How does dropshipping work?

The system is based on a three-party system, you, your customer and your supplier. Understanding this mechanism is essential before you start.

The dropshipping order process

Here's exactly what happens when someone buys from your store:

  • Step 1 : A customer visits your webshop and order a product at 49€
  • Step 2 : You receive the order notification with the payment of 49€
  • Step 3 : You send the order to your supplier and you pay the purchase price (for example 25€)
  • Step 4 : The supplier prepares the package and ships it directly to your customer's address
  • The €24 difference between sale and purchase is before advertising, shipping, fees, returns and taxes.

The customer usually does not know that you are dropshipping. For him, you are the seller and the person responsible for his buying experience. That's why your role is important in managing customer relationships and tracking orders.

Your real mission in dropshipping

You manage marketing, orders and support. Test product quality and track delivery: delegating shipping does not remove customer-experience checks.

Results depend on the product, offer and execution: acquisition, quality, logistics and customer service must work together.

What are the benefits of dropshipping?

Dropshipping has undeniable advantages, especially if you are new to e-commerce or if you want to quickly test ideas without taking too many risks.

Why do so many people choose this model

  • Limited initial inventory: still budget for the store, samples, advertising tests and working capital.
  • Absence of stock : No more warehouses, dormant inventory and unsold products that cost you money
  • Rapid product testing : You can launch a new product in a few hours and remove it just as quickly if it doesn't work
  • Total flexibility : Work from where you want, when you want. Everything is managed from a computer and a internet connection
  • Gradual growth: check that your supplier, cash flow and support can handle the volume.

Prepare a separate test budget for the store, samples and advertising, plus a reserve for suppliers, returns and payment delays. Set your maximum acceptable loss before launching.

An ideal model for experimentation

The real strength of dropshipping is the possibility of testing different products, different niches and different audiences without heavy commitment. You can quickly rotate if something doesn't work. This agility is valuable, especially at the beginning when you are still looking for your place in the market.

The disadvantages you should definitely know

Let's be honest: dropshipping is not a magic bullet. It presents real challenges that you have to anticipate in order not to get stuck.

The real challenges of the model

  • Variable margins: no inventory does not guarantee profit; calculate all costs.
  • Delivery times depend on the supplier, stock, destination and shipping service. Order samples and measure the actual lead time before promising it to customers.
  • Quality checks required: test samples and check each product’s compliance.
  • Fierce competition : A lot of dropshippers sell the same products. Differentiating yourself is becoming a real challenge
  • Dependence on the supplier : If your supplier is out of stock or increases prices, your business is directly impacted

Experts agree on one thing: product quality is non-negotiable. You can't build a sustainable business by selling poor products, even with the best marketing in the world. Ordering samples and testing the products yourself is a must.

The reality of margins and profitability

First sales, profitability and a regular income are separate milestones. Their timing depends on product, budget and execution; no schedule or income is guaranteed.

Is dropshipping legal in France and around the world?

In France, dropshipping follows e-commerce rules. For every target country, check consumer law, taxes, imports and product compliance.

Your legal obligations as a dropshipper

You remain the seller responsible to customers. Requirements depend on your country of establishment and target markets. Related reading: legal framework for dropshipping.

These points apply to a business established in France; requirements differ in other countries.

  • In France: register a business with a suitable legal form.
  • In France: obtain required business identifiers, including SIRET.
  • Display your full legal information on your site (company name, address, contact, terms and conditions)
  • Withdrawal right: in France, generally 14 days from receipt, subject to statutory exceptions.
  • Provide after-sales service and manage returns, even if the problem comes from the supplier

From a fiscal point of view, you must:

  • Declare your income and pay your social security contributions
  • VAT: identify the applicable regime based on establishment, customer, thresholds and delivery flows.
  • IOSS: optional VAT simplification for eligible distance sales imported into the EU, consignments ≤€150, excluding excise goods.

The confusion often comes from the fact that some dropshippers neglect these obligations to get started more quickly. Don't make this mistake: the penalties can be severe and you risk losing everything if you are not in good standing.

The question of responsibility

It is you, and you alone, who are responsible to the end customer. If the package never arrives, if the product is faulty or if the customer wants a refund, they will turn to you. Not to the Chinese supplier that you don't even know personally.

This responsibility implies having an irreproachable after-sales service, answering questions quickly and treating complaints seriously. This is what will make the difference between a business that lasts and a business that collapses at the first problem.

The time for “easy money” is over, but opportunities exist for those who are seriously committed.

What budget does it take to start dropshipping?

Prepare a separate test budget for the store, samples and advertising, plus a reserve for suppliers, returns and payment delays. Set your maximum acceptable loss before launching.

How long until the first results?

First sales, profitability and a regular income are separate milestones. Their timing depends on product, budget and execution; no schedule or income is guaranteed.

What products work best?

Calculate the balance after all costs: delivered product, acquisition, payments, returns, subscriptions and applicable taxes. Use a consistent tax basis; no price multiplier guarantees profit.

Examples of categories that work well: pet accessories, wellness and health products, innovative home gadgets, smartphone and tech accessories, niche beauty products. The classic mistake: choosing a product just because you like it personally. The real question is: is there a proven demand for this product?

How do I manage returns and customer service?

In France, withdrawal generally applies for 14 days from receipt, with exceptions including certain personalised products. Distinguish withdrawal, defects and non-conformity; a partial refund does not replace statutory rights.

The key: communicate transparently with your customers about delivery times right from the start. A lot of problems come from customers who are frustrated with waiting 3 weeks when they thought they would receive their order in 3 days.

Should I create a brand or just resell?

Both approaches work, but brand building is more sustainable. Doing pure dropshipping (without branding) makes you replaceable: anyone can sell the same product as you tomorrow. Creating a brand (logo, history, visual identity, coherent communication) allows you to retain your customers, justify higher prices, and build a valuable asset.

The ideal: start with classic dropshipping to validate the product and the market, then gradually build your brand by improving packaging, communication andcustomer experience.

Dropshipping or e-commerce with stock: what to choose?

Dropshipping reduces initial inventory investment but retains advertising, supplier and cash-flow risks. Holding stock can provide more logistics control, with unsold-inventory risk.

The classic trajectory of e-commerce entrepreneurs: starting with dropshipping to learn and test, then switch to a hybrid or stock-based model once profitability has been proven. Don't see dropshipping as an end in itself, but as a step towards a stronger business.

The benefits of dropshipping

Dropshipping is a model that appeals to a large number of people because of its apparent simplicity. But beyond marketing, some advantages are really differentiating for those who know how to exploit them.

Low initial costs to start a business

You don't need 10,000 euros to create an online business site. This sales method eliminates the massive investment in merchandise. Your budget focuses on three essential items:

  • The creation of your website and your domain name
  • Your advertising spend (Google Ads, social networks)
  • Management and analysis tools

Concretely, you can start with 500 to 1500€ to test your first winning product. This is incomparable with traditional commerce, which often requires several thousand euros in inventory. This solution has existed for years and has allowed many people to get started without a significant initial fund.

The lack of stock management that frees up your cash flow

Is it the wholesaler or the supplier who ensures storage and direct delivery to your buyer. You only pay for the goods after you have collected the order. This system protects your cash flow and drastically reduces financial risk.

No warehouse for rent. No unsold products that lie dormant. No money locked in. This flexibility allows for rapid pivoting if a product does not work. In general, successful stores test between 20 and 50 references before finding their best seller.

A wide range of products without constraints

You can offer hundreds of references for sale in your catalog without ever having them in hand. This ability to test new products quickly is a major strategic advantage.

The process becomes simple: a product does not sell, you remove it. A new trend is emerging, you can add it in a few clicks. This agility allows you to explore different dropshipping niches and to find the market that corresponds to your target. This is the reason why this type of business attracts so many entrepreneurs.

Total geographic flexibility

Your dropshipping business works from anywhere in the world. A computer and an internet connection are sufficient. You manage your customer service, your social media campaigns and your own site from Bali as well as from France.

This freedom attracts a lot of traders looking for independence. But be careful: it requires strong personal discipline. Without a framework, the error of procrastinating awaits every salesperson.

Simplified scalability

When your store starts to generate volume, you have no logistical constraints related to shipping. Placing 10 to 100 orders per day does not change anything in your organization. Your supplier partner absorbs the burden and ships each package directly to the customer.

This scalability allows you to reinvest your profits in the acquisition rather than in fixed costs. It's a virtuous cycle when product and marketing are aligned. You can estimate your growth without worrying about the supply chain.
