The disadvantages of dropshipping

Let's talk cash. Dropshipping is not the El Dorado that some dropshipping courses sell. Here are the real obstacles you need to understand before starting this online business.

A reduced margin that limits your profitability

Profitability depends directly on your margin rate. On average, it oscillates between 15 and 30%. This is low compared to traditional retail where you can reach 50 to 70% with own stock.

Several factors explain these tight margins:

  • You pay more for the product per unit than buying in bulk from a wholesaler
  • Shipping costs are high, especially from Asia
  • Advertising costs explode every year on social networks

The calculation is simple: if your acquisition cost exceeds your margin, you lose money on each sale. That is the number one reason for failure.

Dependence on the supplier

It is the Achilles heel of the business model. You have no control over the quality of the product shipped. If your supplier sends a faulty or poorly packaged package, it's your brand image that hurts. Not hers.

This dependence creates structural fragility. A partner who closes stores or increases prices overnight can put your business at risk. To limit this risk:

  • Always identify a backup provider
  • Order samples regularly to ensure quality
  • Diversify your supply sources as soon as possible

Recurring delivery time issues

Deadlines remain the black spot in dropshipping. With Asian suppliers, it takes 7 to 15 days on average for each package. Sometimes more, especially during periods of high demand such as in October before the holidays. In a world where Amazon delivers in 24 hours, this is a real disadvantage for the customer experience.

These problems lead to customer service tickets, refunds and negative reviews. To avoid this risk, some dropshippers work with European warehouses. The delay increases to 3-5 days but the costs are increasing. It is an increasingly widespread practice in France.

Almost non-existent control over the quality of the product

You are selling a product that you have often never seen or touched. It's a tough bet. Supplier photos do not always reflect reality. The finishes can vary from one lot to another, which is a problem for building loyalty.

Experts recommend that you always order each item before putting it on sale. This allows you to verify quality, create authentic content and better answer the questions of each buyer. It is an investment that avoids many mistakes.

The risk of running out of stock

Your supplier doesn't always let you know when a product is unavailable. You keep selling, orders come in, and you find out the problem last. The result: unhappy customers and forced repayments that impact your cash flow.

This risk is amplified during peak sales. Top sellers automate the synchronization of inventory with their partners. Or they maintain a small buffer stock on their bestsellers to ensure continuity.

Complicated management of returns and the right of withdrawal

Dropshipping returns are a logistical headache. Is your customer sending the product home? At the supplier? Who pays the fees? The right of withdrawal imposes a period of 14 days, which complicates the processing.

This complex management discourages a lot of beginners. The most common solution: offer a partial refund with no return for small amounts. This is often less expensive than managing the reverse supply chain. Be sure to know your legal obligations before defining your policy.

How does dropshipping work?

The system follows a simple three-step process that every trader should understand.

  1. Customer order : a buyer places an order on your store and you collect the payment at the selling price you have set
  2. Transmission : you send the order to your supplier with the delivery information
  3. shipping : the supplier sends the package directly to the end customer via direct delivery

You focus on your marketing strategy, the management of your website and customer service. It is a model where your expertise should lie in acquisition via social networks and conversion, not in logistics. The idea is to become an expert in online sales, not warehouse management.

Is dropshipping legal ?

Yes, dropshipping is legal. This commercial activity exists and is governed by commercial law around the world like any online sale.

However, you must respect several obligations:

  • Clearly display your legal notices on your website
  • Respect the 14-day right of withdrawal
  • Inform about actual delivery times
  • Declare your activity with an adapted legal status
  • Manage VAT and customs if you import from outside the EU

Dropshipping is not a gray area. It is a recognized business practice. The only condition: be transparent with your customers about the deadlines and the origin of the products.

Is it profitable to dropshipping today?

Profitability depends on three key factors: your margin rate, your acquisition cost, and your ability to retain everyone who buys.

The numbers speak for themselves: only 10 to 20% of stores become profitable in the long term. It is no coincidence. The majority fail for several reasons:

  • Lack of differentiation from the competition
  • Margins too low to absorb advertising costs
  • Insufficient initial investment to test enough products
  • Poor customer experience related to deadlines

To generate a real profit, aim for a minimum selling price of x4 on your purchase price. With a product purchased for 10 euros, sell it at least 30€. Below that, your advertising expenses will absorb all your money.

The realistic budget to create a site and launch it? Between 2000 and 5000€. Including 70% in advertising to test a sufficient number of products and audiences on the various networks. It is difficult but not impossible if you have the right method.

Creating an online business site requires following a structured process to avoid classic mistakes.

Step 1: Choose your niche

Analyze demand, competition, and potential margins. Use market analysis tools to identify opportunities. It is the core of your business and it determines 80% of your success.

Step 2: Create your own site

Step 4: Define your marketing strategy

Is dropshipping really right for you?

What abandoned cart recovery strategy really works?

Relaunching is good. But relaunching intelligently with the right method is better. Here's exactly how to structure your follow-up scenario to maximize your chances of recovering lost sales.

The ideal timing to relaunch an abandoned cart

The timings below are a starting point to test, not a universal rule. Adjust them to your buying cycle and customer response.

The timing of the relaunch is 50% of the success of your emailing campaign. Send too soon, you look like a stalker. Send too late, your customer has already purchased elsewhere or has completely forgotten.

The rule of the 3 emails

The method that works best is that of 3 effective reminder emails spaced intelligently:

Follow-up Send Timing Objective Average Open Rate
Email 1 1 hour after abandonment Simple, friendly reminder 45 to 50%
Email 2 24 hours later Reassurance, address concerns 35 to 40%
Email 3 72 hours later Urgency, final incentive 25 to 30%

Why these specific deadlines?

  • 1 hour (followed up within 1 hour): the consumer is still in buying mode. They remember your site and products. Perfect window for a quick, gentle reminder.
  • 24 hours : enough time for him to think, but not enough for him to forget. This is where you need to get rid of his objections with a relevant message.
  • 72 hours : last call. After this date, the chances of conversion drop drastically.

Attention: do not restart for more than 3 days. You are more likely to annoy than convince your prospect.

Email or SMS: which channel should I use?

Email is your main pillar for your communication

For 95% of cases, the reminder email is more than enough. It is:

  • Free (or almost) as a communication solution
  • Easy to automate with any reminder tool
  • Accepted by almost everyone (no need for a phone number)
  • Rich in content (images, call to action, custom text)

SMS, a complement for large baskets

The SMS, reserve it for high-value baskets (above €100 or €150). Why? Because:

  • It costs money every time you send
  • SMS can be highly visible, but measure both performance and customer acceptance
  • Not all your customers have given their number

Example of mixed email + SMS timing

  • Email 1 to 1 hour
  • Email 2 to 24 hours
  • SMS at 48 hours (only if basket > €100)
  • Email 3 to 72 hours

A word about the GDPR

You must have the consent of your customer to send them marketing emails. But good news: an abandoned cart email can be considered transactional (linked to a specific consumer action), so you can often send it even without a marketing opt-in according to the GDPR. However, check this legal notice with a lawyer to be calm in managing the customer relationship.

What are the best practices for relaunching effectively?

Knowing when to send your emails is good. Knowing what to put in to create an engaging email is better. Here are the things that really make the difference between an ignored message and a message that converts.

The essential elements of a reminder email

1. A subject that makes you want to open

The subject of your email is your first impression of the recipient. If it sucks, your email ends up in the trash without even being opened.

Examples of effective topics:

  • “You forgot something 😊”
  • “[First name], your basket is still waiting for you”
  • “We keep your basket warm”
  • “Oops, you left too fast!”

Avoid overly commercial items like “EXCEPTIONAL OFFER ON YOUR BASKET”. It smells like spam from miles away.

2. The basket reminder

Your prospect may have visited a high number of websites during the day. He may no longer remember exactly what he put in your basket. Show him in detail:

  • The image of the product (s)
  • The exact name
  • The unit price
  • The total amount

The more visual the better. A beautiful product image is better than a long text to increase the chances of conversion.

3. A clear and visible call to action

Your call to action (action button) is what makes your customer go from “oh yes, I remember” to “ok, I'm finalizing my order”.

Examples of effective calls to action:

  • “Finalize my order”
  • “Retrieve my basket”
  • “I confirm my purchase”
  • “Complete my purchase now”

Place your call to action at the top AND bottom of the email. Some will read the whole message, others will want to click directly.

4. The elements of reinsurance to improve the customer experience

This is often where your consumer has blocked their online purchase. He had a doubt. Your job is to reassure him through relevant communication.

Items to include:

  • Delivery costs (especially if it's free)
  • Return policy (30 days money back guarantee)
  • Secure payment methods
  • Customer reviews (if you have any)

Perfect reminder email checklist

  • ✅ Personalized and engaging object
  • ✅ Image of the discontinued product
  • ✅ Price and total amount visible
  • ✅ Clear CTA at the top and bottom
  • ✅ Reinsurance elements (delivery, returns, payment)
  • ✅ Friendly and caring tone
  • ✅ No excessive pressure

Should we offer a discount code?

This is THE question that everyone is asking themselves in the e-commerce sector. And the answer is not so simple depending on your project.

Avoid the discount code in the first email

If you systematically offer a discount from the first reminder email, you are conditioning your prospects. They will learn to abandon their shopping cart on purpose to get a promotion. The result: you burn your margins and you create bad habits.

When to use it smartly

Save the promo code for the third email, the last chance email. At this point:

  • You already tried to convince without discount
  • The customer is really hesitant
  • A little push can change the decision and increase your conversion.

Examples of relevant promo codes and personalized offers

  • 10% discount
  • Offer delivery costs
  • Free gift in the package
  • Code valid for 24 hours only (emergency)

The trap to avoid

Don't fall into the trap of “20% immediate discount on all carts”. You are turning your business into a permanent cash register. Book big Black Friday deals or specific events.

Your objective is to sell at full price thanks to the quality of your product, your service and your communication. No systematic trading.

How can you sustainably reduce the cart abandonment rate?

Relaunching via advice to relaunch is good. But avoiding abandonment from the start with tips to reduce the abandonment rate is even better for optimizing the customer journey. Here's how to improve your conversion rate at the source.

1. Simplify your payment process to improve the user experience

Each additional step in your order tunnel on your website is a possibility of losing your prospect. Reduce steps and fields to the minimum needed to complete payment.

Ideal steps for your user journey:

  • Basket
  • Delivery information
  • Payment

What scares consumers away:

  • Obligation to create an account before buying
  • Forms that are too long (10+ fields to fill in)
  • Pages that load slowly on the internet
  • Too many different steps before payment

Simple solution to optimize the customer journey:

Activate the “guest checkout”. Your consumer can create an account after their online purchase if they wish.

2. Show shipping costs early in the journey

Nothing annoys more than an Internet user who discovers a high number of delivery costs when paying. This is the number one reason for shopping cart abandonment on the internet.

Best practices for identifying and overcoming this barrier:

  • Show detailed fees on the product page
  • Indicate the amount for free delivery (“Only 20€ left to give free shipping!”)
  • If possible, offer delivery (and increase your prices slightly to compensate)

3. Reassure from the shopping cart page to improve the experience

Your prospect has doubts. Anticipate them and reassure him before he leaves to increase your conversion.

Reinsurance items to display on your online store:

  • Secure payment badges
  • Clear return policy
  • Visible customer reviews
  • Live chat or FAQ accessible to respond quickly
  • Precise delivery times

4. Optimized for mobile and application

A significant share of ecommerce purchases is made on mobile. If your website is slow or poorly adapted on a smartphone, you lose sales. The mobile user experience is critical.

Mobile checklist to optimize the experience:

  • Responsive site (adapts to all screen sizes)
  • Buttons big enough to be clicked easily
  • Simplified forms (autofill enabled)
  • Fast loading, measured on the devices your customers actually use

5. Offers various payment methods

Some consumers prefer PayPal, others Apple Pay, and still others the bank card. The more options you have, the fewer leads you lose.

Payment methods to offer at least on your website:

  • Bank card (Visa, Mastercard)
  • PayPal
  • Apple Pay/Google Pay
  • Klarna or Alma (payment in several installments)

6. Use an emergency timer (in moderation)

What elements should you test first on your store?

Forget the color of the button. In CRO, the 80/20 rule applies thoroughly: a few well-chosen tests report more than dozens of micro-adjustments. The challenge is prioritizing ideas.

The price (the most underrated test)

Pricing can materially affect conversion, average order value, and margin. It is worth testing when the hypothesis is clear, but no single lever is always the most profitable for every store.

Do not judge a pricing or offer test on conversion rate alone. Compare profit per visitor when cost data is available; otherwise track at least revenue per visitor, AOV, and margin. A higher price may lower conversion while improving the business result, or do the opposite.

The delivery and checkout offer

“Free delivery over 49€” or “Free delivery everywhere” or “Delivery at 4.90€”? These options radically change your AOV (average basket).

The free-shipping threshold is a delicate control. Set it too low and margin falls; set it too high and more shoppers may abandon their carts. Test payment options that suit your audience without assuming one universal basket threshold.

The hero image on your product sheet (above the waterline)

The first visual on a product page affects how quickly shoppers understand the offer. Test lifestyle images, packshots, video, or carousels and measure the outcome; no fixed conversion lift applies to every store.

Call to action and social proof

“Order now”, “I want it”, “Add to cart”. Three button texts, three different levels of engagement. The wording of the button is one of the simplest content tests to set up.

The position of social proof is as important as its content. Notes, number of reviews, trust badges: bringing these elements closer to the purchase button via a layout test can be enough to unlock a few conversion points. A sticky button on mobile also helps to reduce the bounce rate, especially on long pages.

The structure of your homepage and landing pages

FAQ at the top or at the bottom? Customer reviews above or below the buy button? Impossible to answer without testing. Each niche reacts differently. Start a layout test or a landing page test for your brand and let the data answer.

Install a heatmap on your high-traffic pages. You'll see exactly how your visitors behave: where they click, where they pick up, and what they're completely unaware of. This type of data guides your hypotheses much better than intuition.

How to A/B test on Shopify in 5 steps

1. Formulate a precise hypothesis

Start with a problem observed in your own data. Example: “My add-to-cart rate is 4%. I think a product-use video may improve it because it addresses an objection found in customer feedback.”

The structure that works: “If I change [item], then [metric] goes [direction] because [reason].” Without it, you won't be able to interpret your results.

2. Install your A/B testing tool and configure tracking

The installation is done from the Shopify App Store. The three tools in the table offer a free trial or a free plan to get started for free.

The classic trap: poorly configured tracking. Place a fictional order to verify that the tool registers each command in the correct variant. Connect it to your analytics (Shopify or Google Analytics) to track conversions and track metrics that matter. A test with false data is worse than no test at all.

3. Create your two variants (no more)

Variant A: your current page. Your control group. Variant B: only one modification.

Change one element per test when you need to attribute the effect to that change. Multivariate tests create more combinations and require more data; use a sample-size calculation rather than an arbitrary monthly-traffic threshold.

4. Define your sample size before launching

Calculate sample size before launch using your current rate, minimum detectable effect, confidence level, and statistical power. The required volume can be far below or far above 1,000 visitors per variant.

5. Start and don't touch anything

It's honestly the hardest part of the process. You will want to look at the results after 24 hours and to cut as soon as a variant “seems” winning. Don't fall into this trap: the initial fluctuations mean nothing. Let it run up to your predefined sample size, not an hour before.

Analyzing the results of an A/B test: statistical significance and metrics

In a frequentist analysis with a 5% threshold, a result is statistically significant when its p-value is below 0.05. This does not mean there is exactly a 95% chance that the variant wins; also assess effect size and business value.

Pitfalls to avoid when analyzing your tests

Peeking and stopping as soon as one variant appears ahead raise the risk of a false conclusion under a conventional frequentist analysis. Follow the stopping rule set by your tool and experiment plan; sequential and Bayesian methods require their own interpretation.

Run the test through at least one full business cycle, including weekday and weekend behavior, and continue until the planned sample is reached. Seven days is not automatically enough when the required volume is missing.

What metric should I follow?

Read conversion rate alongside average order value. For price or offer changes, profit per visitor is often more useful than revenue per visitor alone because it reflects margin.

If variant B converts 5% less but produces a 15% higher AOV, revenue per visitor may rise. Check the calculation, margin, statistical uncertainty, and side effects before declaring a winner.

Also review abandonment, call-to-action clicks, and funnel steps. These metrics help explain a result, but higher time on page alone does not prove what caused conversion.

Mistakes that are sabotaging your A/B testing results

Testing without enough traffic

With low traffic, test a change large enough to create a useful and realistic effect. Still calculate the sample you need: low volume does not become conclusive simply because the variants are farther apart.

Edit a test along the way

If you adjust your B variant in the middle of the test, your data is contaminated and you have no choice but to stop and restart a new test.

Ignore the flicker effect on your website

Flicker can change behavior and hurt the experience. Review the tool's anti-flicker or server-side options, then measure the actual effect on your store and Core Web Vitals instead of assuming all impact disappears.

Forget segmentation by buying behavior

An overall result can hide differences by device, traffic source, or new versus returning visitors. Define these segments before the test and interpret them carefully because each split reduces sample size.

Do not document your tests

Keep a record of the date, hypothesis, tested element, analysis plan, result, and learning. This documentation prevents repeated tests and preserves the context behind decisions.

A/B testing on Shopify is an ongoing process!

Make testing part of your routine at a pace set by traffic and required sample size. Some stores can conclude several experiments a month; others need fewer, longer tests.

Tool costs vary, and available traffic limits what a store can conclude. Start with one high-priority test only when the planned sample is reachable.

Look at the opinions of other retailers before making your choice. An application with less than 4 stars deserves your distrust. Also, check the date of the last update to ensure that the developer takes care of the regular fixes and improvements.

Configure the essential settings: color widget, number of reviews displayed, and sorting option. The design should integrate naturally into your website without distracting the visitor who wants to buy on the page.

Also remember to configure the language if your store targets a French-speaking audience. Displaying reviews that are consistent with the rest of your store reinforces the credibility of your business.

Step 5: Activate notifications and request emails

Program the automatic sending of review emails after each delivery. 7-14 days after shipping works well. The customer had time to test the product without forgetting the purchase.

The technical fundamentals to be respected

The speed of your website determines your SEO. Google penalizes sites that take more than 3 seconds to load. This degraded user experience directly impacts your conversions. Compress your images, use the WebP format, limit third-party applications that weigh down your site.

Siloed architecture improves search engine crawling. Organize your categories logically: each category groups together similar products, linked together by internal links. Schema.org markup tells search engines the nature of your pages and allows you to get rich results (stars, prices, stock). This semantic optimization is essential to appear in featured snippets.

On-page optimization for dropshipping

How to optimize your product page

Your product page must respond immediately to the intention of the Internet user. Start with a clear title that integrates your main keyword and the product benefit. The user experience starts with the title.

Your description should be at least 300 words of unique text. And above all, don't stupidly copy the AliExpress supplier descriptions that 50 other shops already use. This practice penalizes you heavily in terms of SEO. Rewrite while focusing on concrete benefits for your customer. Add descriptive alt tags to each visual to attract traffic via Google Images.

For example, instead of “Dog use,” write “Anti-pull dog tap into: control and comfort while walking for Labrador.” This semantic approach enriches your content and better targets requests.

  • FAQ to catch frequently asked questions
  • Customer review section with visible overall rating
  • Video support or customer photos to enrich the experience

The FAQ is a real booster for your SEO. Google often shows these questions and answers directly in the results. This solution makes it possible to capture additional traffic on long-tail requests.

Optimize your category pages

Category pages generate massive traffic to your store. Add an introduction text of 200 words at the top of the page and 400 to 600 words below the product grid. Write a real buying guide, as if you were a salesperson in a store.

This setup turns a page only full of products into a useful page for your visitors and for Google.

Structure with clear filters: size, color, price, customer rating. Set filter URLs to “noindex” to avoid duplicate content. This technical management is essential to preserve your crawl budget.

SEO content strategy for dropshipping

Why start a blog?

Blogging is your secret weapon for generating organic traffic. It allows you to position yourself on hundreds of informational queries that your product page cannot capture.

Content marketing builds your thematic authority on the web and can sometimes generate natural backlinks.

This approach will allow you to share your expertise and create a real brand in your sector. The advantage of a blog is that it attracts visitors before they make a purchase decision.

How do I find the right topics?

There are several tools to identify trends in your sector. For example, Google Trends shows you how searches have changed over time. This analysis will allow you to create content at the right time.

Structure of an SEO optimized article

Always use the inverted pyramid concept. Your introduction should answer the title question immediately. Use clear H2 and H3 subtitles Internet users scan more than they actually read the text.

Aim for 1500 to 2500 words for the main articles. For more targeted topics, 800 to 1200 words are sufficient. Information density matters more than pure volume. This editorial practice improves your positioning.

Publish at least 2 to 3 articles per week at the start. This consistency shows search engines that your site is active. Update your old content every 6 months with the mention “Updated January 2025". This update reinforces your credibility with the algorithm.

Also include video when relevant. The video format enhances the user experience and increases the time spent on your page, a positive signal for Google.

Off-page SEO and domain authority

Why are backlinks important?

Backlinks are the web's votes of confidence. The more quality links you accumulate, the more your domain authority increases. In dropshipping SEO, authority makes all the difference compared to competitors who sell the same products but with less authority.

A link from a recognized blog in your field is much better than 100 links from rotten sites from Fiverr sellers. The Google algorithm penalizes link profiles that look unnatural.

Accessible netlinking strategies

Netlinking consists of getting inbound links to your site. Here are the top strategies for dropshippers:

  • Guest blogging: pitch guest articles to 10-20 blogs in your niche in exchange for a link to your dropshipping site. You share expertise and earn backlinks.
  • Digital press relations : contact journalists with case studies or exclusive statistics. This strategy requires more work but provides real credibility.
  • Quality directories : register on specialized e-commerce directories. Prioritize quality over quantity
  • Ninjalinking : place your link on forums or as a comment on blogs on your topic. This practice works if you bring real value
  • Buying links : Several online platforms connect buyers and sellers of links

The use of social networks also helps to share your content and create opportunities for connections.

Focus on Instagram and TikTok if your target audience is young. These platforms generate direct traffic that improves your user signals. The social network is becoming an effective distribution medium for your content.

Reviews generate fresh content on a regular basis. Integrate them with Schema Review markup to show stars in Google results. This semantic optimization drastically improves your click rate.

Ask your satisfied customers 7 days after delivery with a direct link to the review form. This proactive management of reviews will allow you to build your social proof quickly.

Fatal mistakes to avoid

Mistake #1: Giving up after 10 videos

The trap : “I posted 10 videos, it doesn't work, organic is a scam”

The reality : The TikTok algorithm needs 20-30 videos to understand your audience. The first 15 videos are used to “educate” the algorithm.

The solution : Commit to 30 days/60 videos minimum before judging. Note everything: views, completion, bio clicks. The patterns are revealed after 20+ videos.

Mistake #2: Wanting to make “perfect” content

The trap : Spend 3 hours editing a TikTok video with transitions, effects, perfect music

The reality : “Raw” TikTok videos (shot on an iPhone in one take) often perform better. Authenticity > perfection.

The solution : Limit yourself to 15 minutes max per video. Movie → Light trim → Subtitles → Post. Speed beats quality organic. Mistake #3: Ignoring analytics

Mistake #3: Not analyzing your results

The trap : Post in “spray and pray” mode without analyzing what works

The reality : 80% of your results will come from 20% of your content. If you don't track, you'll never know what to overtake.

The solution : Each week, identify your 2 most efficient videos (views + organic clicks). Do 3 variations of these formats the following week.

Mistake #4: Neglecting Customer Service

The trap : “It's just dropshipping, I'm sending and it's good”

The reality : Organic traffic generates 2-3x more questions than ad traffic. People want to be reassured.

The solution : Respond to ALL Tiktok/Instagram comments within 2 hours. Add a live chat to your site (free Tidio). Good after-sales service = customers who share = word-of-mouth = more organic sales.

Mistake #5: Selling an “average” product

The trap : “Organically I can sell anything if I make good videos”

The reality : A viral video about a mediocre product = 100 sales then negative feedback and reviews that kill your brand.

The solution : ALWAYS order your product before selling it. Test it for 7 days. If you don't use it yourself, you won't sell it organically.

FAQ: The most asked questions

Is it really possible to do dropshipping without an advertising budget?

Yes, but with 2 nuances:

  1. You need a mini startup budget : €200-500 to buy your domain name, your Shopify theme, order samples, and possibly a product analysis tool like Minea (€30/month).
  2. You trade money for time: instead of €3,000 on Facebook Ads, invest 2-3 hours a day for 60 days creating content. Can't hold that pace? Organic isn't for you.

What niche works best organically?

Niches that are exploding organically :

  • Wellness/pain : ergonomic cushions, posture correctors, massagers
  • Kitchen/gadgets : tools that make a boring task easier
  • Decor/LED : visual transformations of rooms
  • Animals : accessories, toys, care
  • Home fitness : rubber bands, compact devices
  • Beauty/skincare : tools (face rollers, LED masks)

Niches to avoid : fashion/clothing (too many returns), tech/electronics (low margins), jewelry (saturated), non-validated “health” products (shadowban TikTok).

Do you have to show your face?

No, but it helps a lot. Face videos generate +40% engagement on TikTok.

Alternatives if you don't want to show up :

  • Voiceover with product video
  • Hands only (demonstration)
  • Customer testimonies filmed by them
  • “ASMR” format (no voice, just product noises)
  • Text + product animation

The best compromise : Show yourself in 1 out of 3 videos (the ones that “tell” your why). The others may be faceless demos.

Does TikTok block product videos?

Not if you do it well. TikTok doesn't block “product videos,” it blocks “disguised ads.”

What's going on :

  • Video that provides value (tutorial, tip, problem solving)
  • Natural, not commercial tone
  • Product shown in real use

What is shadowban :

  • Video shot in the studio with white background (= advertising content)
  • Text-to-speech robot voice that says “Click on the link in bio”
  • Product presented as a classic advertisement
  • Too aggressive call to action in the first 3 seconds

The rule : 90% value, 10% sales. Give first, sell later.

Can we do that from France/Belgium/Belgium/Canada?

Yes, organic dropshipping works in all French-speaking countries.

Special features by country :

  • france : Huge market, strong competition, delivery from Europe recommended (7-10 days vs 20+ days China)
  • belgium : Smaller but less saturated market, easy EU delivery
  • morocco : Excellent margin because living costs are low, but pay attention to delivery times (15-25 days)
  • canada : Interesting market, remember to also target the US market (English) to scale

tip : If you are in Canada, build 2 shopify stores (1 French + 1 English speaking) and double your videos in both languages.

How much time per day should you devote to it?

Launch phase (days 1-30) : 2-3 hours/day

  • 1h: content creation (shoot 2-3 videos)
  • 30min: Pinterest + Reels programming
  • 30min: reply to comments + DM
  • 30min: performance analysis + adjustments

  • 30min: 1 video/day
  • 30min: feedback management + after-sales service
  • 30min: site optimizations + new products

Automation possible after 60 days : Outsource content creation to a video editor (50-100€/month for 20 videos). You only keep the strategy and the after-sales service.

What is the minimum budget to start?

Minimal startup budget : €300-500

  • Shopify: €1 for 3 months (trial offer), then €30/month

How do I manage multiple platforms at the same time?

The optimal repurposing system :

  1. Centralized creation : Film 3 TikTok videos on Monday (1h batch recording)
  2. Automatic distribution :
    • Monday: Video post 1 on TikTok
    • Tuesday: Repurpose video 1 on Reels + Shorts
    • Wednesday: Turn 1 video into 3 Pinterest pins
    • Thursday: Video Post 2 on TikTok
    • Friday: Repurpose video 2 on Reels + Shorts

    • Sunday: Performance analysis + next week schedule

  • Later (Instagram + Pinterest line-up)

Will I have enough traffic to make a living from this?

Realistic benchmark after 90 days of organic :

  • TikTok: 50K-200K views/month
  • Instagram: 20K-80K views/month
  • Pinterest: 5K-20K visits/month
  • Total: 75K-300K prints/month

Typical conversion :

  • 1% of impressions click on your link = 750-3000 site visits/month
  • 2% of visits buy = 15-60 sales/month
  • Average basket 30€ = 450€-1800€ CA/month

To live comfortably (3000€+/month) :

  • Objective: 100 sales/month with an average basket of €30 = €3,000 CA
  • With a 50% margin = 1500€ net
  • Need 5000 site visits/month (2% conversion rate)
  • That is 250K-500K organic prints/month

This can be achieved in 3-4 months with a solid strategy.

What should I do if my first video doesn't work?

Don't panic. Statistically, only 1 out of 10 videos exceeds 10K views.

Diagnostic checklist :

Weak hook : Are the first 3 seconds intriguing? Test 5 different hooks on the same content.

Bad timing : Did you post at 3am? Repost the same video at 6pm-9pm (primetime TikTok).

Video quality : Blurry video or saturated sound? Shoot in full natural light, stabilize your phone.

Call to action absent : Aren't you saying what to do next? Add “Link in bio” in the subtitles AND in voiceover.

Wrong hashtags : Do you put #fyp #pourtoi (useless)? Use niche hashtags: #cuisinefacile #astucemaison #ideocadeau.

The 20-video rule : Do not draw any conclusions before 20 videos. Some accounts take off on video 3, others on video 25.

Do organic products work as well as ads?

Ads = speed. The organic = endurance.

Facebook Ads :

  • Immediate results (sales from day 1)
  • Precise targeting
  • High customer acquisition cost (20-40€)
  • Total dependence on the platform
  • Risk of an account being banned

Organic :

  • Acquisition cost = 0€
  • Cumulative traffic over time
  • Stronger customer relationship
  • Slower results (3-4 weeks)
  • Request for regularity

The ideal : Start organically to validate the product + generate cash. Then inject this cash into ads to scale x5-10. This is the strategy of brands that make 50K+/month.

Choosing a supplier makes all the difference between a profitable store and a logistical nightmare. TikTok Shop imposes high standards on order processing: fast shipping, consistent quality, and responsive customer service for each customer.

The effective way to find suppliers

Start your research on B2B platforms like Alibaba, Global Sources, or 1688. Type the name of your product followed by “dropshipping supplier” or “white label.” Contact at least 10 to 15 suppliers to compare their offers and find the right partner.

Essential questions to ask at the first contact when choosing a supplier:

  • MOQ (minimum order quantity) : minimum quantity per order to get the best prices
  • Production lead time : time between order and shipping to see if it fits
  • Shipping options : carriers available, delivery times by country for fast shipping
  • Branding possibility : packaging customization, logo, inserts for your brand
  • Decreasing prices : discounts according to volumes to generate more money
  • Return policy : management of defective products that sometimes arrive

Every question is answered precisely by a serious dropshipping supplier. Vague answers or long response times signal a lack of professionalism. It's better to try a different provider.

Use a tracking file to compare your dropshipping suppliers. Note the unit price, shipping costs, announced deadlines, responsiveness and sample quality. This organization is useful and saves you a lot of time in the long run.

Sourcing agent or direct supplier?

You have two main options for your product sourcing: working directly with a factory or going through a sourcing agent. Each method has its advantages depending on your situation and your level of experience.

Sourcing agent:

  • Act as an intermediary between you and the factories to simplify the process
  • Negotiate prices and check quality for you every day
  • Manage the fulfillment and shipping process from A to Z
  • Suitable if you sell several different products on your store
  • Compare several suppliers, samples, delivery times and total costs before choosing.

Direct supplier:

  • Better unit prices without intermediaries to generate more profit
  • Direct relationship with the manufacturer that allows more control
  • Less flexibility on small quantities at the beginning
  • You manage the quality controls yourself, which takes time
  • Suitable for a single product sold in volume

To start your dropshipping business on TikTok Shop, an agent simplifies the process considerably. Some agents even offer warehouses in Europe for fast shipping. The additional cost is justified because you save time and avoid a lot of problems.

Guarantee the high quality of your products

Product quality determines your reputation on TikTok Shop. A single batch of faulty products can generate a wave of negative reviews that are impossible to catch up with. The winning mindset: consider quality as an investment that will pay off, not a cost.

Recommended quality control process for your dropshipping:

  1. Ordering samples : try 3 to 5 units before ordering in bulk
  2. Visual inspection : check the finishes, the stitching, the materials to see the quality
  3. Usage test : use the product as a customer would for several days
  4. Feedback from the surroundings : get tested by people from your target audience to get reviews
  5. Test command : place a real order to check the complete itinerary
  6. Regular follow-up : recommends samples every 2-3 months to check that the quality remains high

Clearly communicate your quality standards to your dropshipping supplier. Request photos and videos of each lot before shipping. This vigilance avoids unpleasant surprises and protects your brand in the long term.

Create advertising content that converts

The first 3 seconds decide the success of your ad. You need to catch on immediately with a strong visual hook, an intriguing question, or a clear promise. The user must stop scrolling instantly to see your content.

Elements of a successful creative that will attract sales:

  • Powerful hook : visual or verbal element in the first 3 seconds that stops the scroll
  • Problem identified : show the frustration your product solves for people
  • Product demonstration : the product in action with immediate visible results
  • Social proof : testimonials, reviews, number of sales to build trust
  • Call to action : clear instruction to buy now, not later

Native formats work better than traditional social media ads. Shoot with your phone instead of professional equipment. Authenticity reassures TikTok users and creates trust. Overly slick ads look suspicious and generate distrust even among interested buyers.

Interest-based targeting is the first place to start. TikTok offers broad categories such as “Beauty”, “Fitness” or “Tech”. Refine progressively based on conversion data. The algorithm learns which people are buying and targeting better over time.

Types of audiences to try for your TikTok Shop dropshipping store:

  • Retargeting : visitors to your store who did not buy the first time

Similar audiences amplify your results once you have enough data. With 100+ buyers, create a similar audience. TikTok will find comparable profiles who are likely to buy as well.

Retargeting can complement cold acquisition. Measure its incremental impact and profitability instead of applying a universal multiplier.

Monitor your CPM (cost per 1000 impressions) and CTR (click through rate) daily. These metrics tell you if your content is getting people's attention. A high CPM with a low CTR means an unengaging creative that needs to be changed quickly.

How do you analyze the performance of your own store?

1. Technical diagnosis (SEO + performance)

If your store is slow, poorly referenced or buggy, regardless of the quality of your products, you are losing money.

The 7 points to check:

1) Charging speed

  • Go On pagespeed.web.dev
  • Enter the URL of your homepage
  • Minimum acceptable score: 70/100 on mobile
  • Under 50? You May Be Losing Sales

The 3 main causes of slowness:

  • Non-optimized images (uses TinyPNG or automatic Shopify)
  • Too Many Apps Installed (Uninstall What You Don't Use)
  • Incorrectly coded theme (sometimes changing the theme solves everything)

2) Core Web Vitals: These Google metrics that can affect your ranking:

  • LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) : must be < 2.5s
  • INP (Interaction to Next Paint): should be 200 ms or less
  • CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift) : must be < 0.1

Check them out in Google Search Console.

3) Architecture URL: Your URLs should be clean:

  • ✅ GOOD: /collections/t-shirts/products/black-t-shirt or /products/black-t-shirt
  • ❌ REVIEW: a parameter-heavy URL without a consistent canonical

Shopify handles this automatically, but check that you don't have any weird settings that pollute.

4) H1 tags/meta titles: Each page should have:

  • 1 single, unique and descriptive H1
  • 1 meta title < 60 characters
  • 1 meta description < 160 characters inviting you to click

5) Content duplications: Just avoid having the same content as your competitors.

6) ALT text images: All of your images should have alternative text describing what we're seeing. Not just “IMG_1234" it should be descriptive and include keywords.

7) Mobile-friendly: check your own mobile share and test the journey on several phones.

2. Shopify Analytics data analysis

The crux of the matter: The numbers never lie. Shopify Analytics gives you everything you need to make smart decisions.

The 5 metrics you MUST track every week:

1) Conversion rate

  • Formula: (Orders/Visitors) ×100
  • E-commerce benchmark: 1-3%
  • < 1%? Offer, Price, or Trust Problem

> 3% You found a winning product, scale it

2) Average basket value (AOV)

  • How much does a customer spend on average?
  • To increase it: bundles, upsells, free shipping over €X
  • Example: if your AOV is €45, offer free delivery at €50. You will see your AOV increase.

3) Card Failed to Give Up

  • The average is 70%
  • If Yours Exceed 75%, It's a Red Flag
  • Solutions: automatic email reminders, simplify the checkout, add payment methods

4) Most profitable acquisition channel

  • Where do your sales come from? Facebook? Google? Instagram? Organic?
  • The Channel That Converts Best - The One That Generates the Most Traffic
  • Concrete example: maybe you have 10K visitors from Facebook but only 50 sales, and 1K visitors from Google with 80 sales → Google is more profitable, focus on it

5) High-performance products VS underperforming

  • Table in Shopify Analytics > Products
  • Sort by “Sales” and “Product Views”
  • If a product has a lot of views but few sales: price, description or photo problem
  • If a product has few views but a good conversion rate: increase your visibility on it (ads, homepage)

The secret of shops that scale: They don't rely on cold traffic to sell. They have automated systems that relaunch, engage, and convert.

Email marketing: the 4 mandatory automated flows

1) Welcome

  • Triggered When Someone Signs Up for Your Newsletter
  • 3 emails 2-3 days apart
  • Email 1: Thank you + welcome promo code (-10%)

  • Email 1: Confirmation + tracking

How does a sourcing agent work? (The 8-step process)

1. Specifications : You explain exactly what you want: dimensions, materials, materials, materials, colors, packaging, necessary certifications. The more specific you are, the better.

2. Search for suppliers : The agent searches his network and in the field for the 3-5 best suppliers for your product.

3. Validation & audit : He visits each factory, checks production capacities, certifications and reliability.

4. Negotiation : It gets the best prices, reduces MOQs, and secures payment terms.

5. Sampling : He orders samples, send them to you, collect your feedback and get them adjusted until it's perfect.

6. Production monitoring : Once the order is launched, he monitors the progress and ensures that the deadlines are respected.

7. Quality inspection : It inspects 100% or a statistical sample of your production according to a strict protocol (AQL).

8. Logistics & customs : He organizes the shipment, manages the customs clearance and ensures that everything arrives in good condition.

2. Do you offer personalized packaging, inserts or private labeling?

  • You Offer Private Label or just basic labelling?
  • Can you put my logo on the product itself?

3. What shipping options do you use and what are the actual delivery times?

You Need to Get Detailed Answers, not just “standard shipping.”

Questions to ask:

  • Which carriers do you use depending on the zone? (France, Europe, USA, Canada...)

Advice: Ask for examples of recent tracking numbers to verify that they are real.

  • What protocol do you follow? (visual inspection, functional tests, AQL...)

Write articles that appeal to Google and your readers

A good ecommerce blog post answers a specific question quickly. The inverted pyramid is a useful editorial method for putting the answer before the detail, not a universal ranking formula.

The inverted pyramid applied to your blog

The principle is in one sentence: start each article and each section with the most important information. Answer the user's question from the first few lines, then detail gradually.

Imagine that a friend asks you which headphones to buy. You're not going to give him a 20-minute talk about the history of high fidelity sound before giving him your recommendation. You tell him “take this one for this purpose” and then you explain why. In writing, it's the same.

Concretely, your article should start with a box or a short paragraph that summarizes the essential points. Then each part goes deeper into one aspect, always starting with the most useful one.

The gain is twofold.

A reader in a hurry reaches the answer faster. This structure can improve readability, but bounce rate also depends on relevance, speed, context and how it is measured.

Setting up Translate & Adapt: Step-by-Step Guide

It takes less than 15 minutes to set up. Here are the steps from your Shopify admin.

  1. Go to Settings > Languages. Click on “Add a language” and select the language you want to translate. Shopify supports over 20 languages natively.
  2. Install the Translate & Adapt app from the Shopify App Store. Open it, pick the language: content shows up by type (product, collection, pages, nav, theme).

Moving from translation to localization

Translation is a technical step. Localization is a business strategy. The difference determines whether you make money with international customers or if you waste your time.

Localizing means adapting the complete user experience:

  • The currencies displayed according to the target country
  • Local payment methods (iDEAL in the Netherlands, Klarna in Germany)
  • Date formats, units of measurement and product sizes
  • Delivery costs and return conditions in accordance with each market

These details seem minor. They make all the difference in the conversion rate.

Shopify Markets makes this approach easy. From your dashboard, you define target markets with specific currencies, languages and domains. The tool takes care of the complete management of your markets without external services. You can even customize market prices to absorb customs fees.

Speed and compatibility: two blind spots

Some translation applications make your website heavier by adding JavaScript scripts. Before choosing a solution, test the impact on your Core Web Vitals. A translated store that takes 5 seconds to load will lose more customers than it gains.

Also, think about adapting your marketing content. Your abandoned cart reminder emails and post-purchase sequences must exist in each language. Every notification sent in the wrong language makes you lose trust.

The ultimate test before publishing

Have your store browse, translated by a native of the target language. Not a French speaker who speaks English. A native English speaker. It will spot awkward turns and cultural inconsistencies that you will never see. Ask them for an honest review of each important page before going into production.

Mistakes to avoid with a dropshipping supplier (the ones that kill your store)

La majority of shops dropshipping closes in the first 6 months.

Mistake #1: Choosing only on price

The trap : You find a €3 product on AliExpress, you sell it for €29, you say to yourself “I'm going to make myself a €26 margin per sale, jackpot!”

The reality :

  • Delivery costs: 5€
  • Refunds (25%): €6.50
  • After-sales service (time spent): 3€
  • Pub (20€ per sale): 20€

Actual margin : -8,50€. You lose money with every sale.

The solution : Always calculate the net margin after ALL costs (delivery, refunds, after-sales service, advertising). If it is < €10, the product is not viable.

Mistake #2: Neglecting supplier after-sales service

The trap : Your supplier takes 7 days to respond to your emails. You say to yourself “no big deal, I manage”.

The reality : Your customer wants an answer NOW. If you wait 7 days for the supplier's response, your customer asks for a PayPal refund or leaves a negative review.

The solution : Test the supplier after-sales service BEFORE launching. Send 3-4 emails with specific questions. If they respond in > 48 hours or with vague answers, flee.

Mistake #3: Ignoring real deadlines

The trap : The supplier announces “7-10 days”, you put “Delivery within 10 days” on your site.

The reality : The announced deadlines are STILL optimistic. Add 30-50% to the announced delay to get the actual delay.

Calculus :

  • Supplier announces 7-10 days
  • Reality: 10-15 days
  • You advertise on your site: “Delivery within 14-21 days”

Why it's important : If you announce 10 days and the customer receives it in 18 days, he asks for a refund. If you announce 21 days and he receives in 15 days, he is pleasantly surprised.

Golden rule : Always over-promise on deadlines. A surprised customer is better than a disappointed one.

Mistake #4: Confusing provider and platform

The trap : Do you think CJ Dropshipping or Spocket are suppliers.

The reality : They are platforms that bring together hundreds of suppliers. The real supplier is the Chinese factory or the European wholesaler behind it.

Why it's important : On CJ, you have 1000 suppliers for the same product. Quality, time and price vary from simple to triple.

The solution : On platforms, always filter by:

  • Supplier Rating (> 4.5/5)
  • Number of orders (> 1000)
  • Warehouse location (EU if you want something fast)
  • Actual delay (read customer reviews)

Mistake #5: Not ordering a sample

The trap : “I'm going to save time, I'm launching directly without testing the product.”

The reality : You get 50 orders, customers get a product different from the photos, 30 refunds, your store is ruined.

The calculation : A sample costs 10-30€. A bad product costs you €500-2,000 in refunds + loss of credibility.

The solution : Always order a sample before launching a product. Test:

  • Real quality vs photos
  • Actual delivery time
  • Packaging (the customer sees it first)
  • Potential problems (poor assembly, chemical smell...)

Ad longevity is a signal, not proof of sales or profitability. Use it to prioritize research, then validate demand, competition, landed cost and a sample.

Mistake #6: Wanting to automate everything from the start

The trap : Two extremes:

  1. You install Dropified, you synchronize 500 products, you launch ads, you wait for sales
  2. You do everything manually for 6 months and you lose 40 hours per week

The reality : You have to process the first 20 orders manually. Why?

  • You detect problem products
  • You optimize your product descriptions

But after 50 sales, you have to automate : Otherwise you will drown in repetitive tasks.

The solution :

  • Weeks 1-4 : Processed manually to understand (20-50 sales)
  • From week 5 : Automated with AutoDS or Dropified
  • AutoDS saves you 15-20h/week on: product import, stock management, orders, pricing, tracking

The calculation : €19.90/month AutoDS vs 20h/week × 4 weeks = 80h/month saved. If your time is worth €15/hour, you earn €1200/month in productivity.

Mistake #7: Not diversifying suppliers

The trap : You find a perfect supplier, you put all your products in his house.

The reality : His warehouse is burning, or he's stopping a product, or he's raising his prices by 40%, or he's ghosting you. And you are stuck.

The solution :

Create a website with a free trial:

  • Shopify: 3 days free then €1/month for 3 months.
  • WooCommerce: free on WordPress.
  • Prestashop: open source.

You can create a dropshipping site for free with any of these CMS.

Add a dropshipping module from the App Store and connect CJ or DSers. The total installation takes a few minutes. Import 5 to 15 products into a targeted niche. Not 50. A handful is enough.

Start your first ad-free sales if your budget is zero. TikTok, Instagram Reels, and Pinterest are still doing well organically. When you generate orders, reinvest 5-10 €/day in advertising marketing. Professionals count on a test budget of €4,000 to €5,000 to find a profitable product. It's an investment, not an expense.

At the beginning, manage the customer service yourself. Call your first buyers. Understand what they expected, what surprised them, what disappointed them. It is this customer knowledge that will make the difference when you want to scale your business.

What products can you dropship for free?

Niche products with high perceived value are the most profitable in e-commerce. A desk accessory purchased €3 on CJ sells for €15-25 in a well-branded dropshipping store. Aim for a minimum coefficient of x3 between purchase price and sale price for a significant margin to be achieved.

Print-on-demand opens up an almost unlimited catalog of products: T-shirts, mugs, posters, cases, personalized photo printing. Zero stock, zero risk.

The white label solution is also available at no initial cost. CJ and Eprolo allow you to put your own name and logo on existing products (cosmetics, supplements, tech accessories). A good way to go from pure dropshipping to creating a brand.

Avoid heavy products (high shipping costs) and those with a margin of less than x3. Below that, your margin won't cover advertising costs.

What platforms offer free dropshipping?

Three types of free dropshipping platforms coexist:

  • E-commerce CMS (Shopify WooCommerce, Prestashop) to create your online store.
  • Dropshipping applications (DSers, CJ, Spocket, Eprolo) to connect suppliers.
  • Marketplaces (eBay, Amazon) to sell without a website, with commissions of 8 to 15%.

The most popular combination: a Shopify site + a free app like CJ or DSers. You control your brand, your prices, your communication. You can track each order and optimize your prices based on returns.

Copyfy allows you to go faster: identify winning products, analyze competing stores, spy on ads that work on social networks. The type of resource that saves you weeks of research.

Find your next winning product for free !

How do you choose a reliable dropshipping supplier?

Order a sample. Always. This is the number one tip for any e-commerce professional. Check the actual quality, packaging, drop delivery time. If the supplier refuses to send a sample, go your way.

Check reviews on the Shopify App Store and Trustpilot. Focus on the recent ones (the older ones no longer reflect reality). Also check its legal address and privacy policy page to make sure it's a real business.

Test customer service before your first order request. Ask a technical question and time the answer. 72 hours to answer a basic question? Imagine when a customer has a real problem.

Also, see how it handles stockouts and returns. The best suppliers warn in advance and offer new products as an alternative. The worst leave you to fend for yourself.

What are the benefits of dropshipping at no cost?

You are starting a dropshipping business with almost zero financial risk. No stock. No storage. The total installation is almost free. It's hard to find a lower entry barrier in e-commerce.

The model is simple: you only pay for the product after receiving payment from the customer.

  • You sell before you buy.
  • You test 10 products in one week without incurring thousands of euros.
  • If it doesn't work, you remove the product.
  • Price optimization is done in real time.
  • You can sell to the UK or other major markets without changing anything.

In terms of margins, let's be direct: 15 to 25% net after advertising. With a European supplier, it's tighter but the conversion rates make up for it thanks to the short deadlines. Your supplier's commercial offer and delivery services have a direct impact on the success of your business.

What delivery times can you expect?

Origin Delivery time to France Suppliers
France 1 to 3 days Syncee (EU suppliers)
Europe 3 to 7 days Spocket, Printful
USA 7 to 15 days Zendrop, Eprolo, Trendsi
China (standard) 15 to 25 days AliExpress/DSers, PlusBuyer
China (express) 7 to 12 days CJ Dropshipping, Wiio

The strategy that works: dropshipping tests from China. As soon as a product works, store 50-100 units in European warehouses. You go from 15 days to 3 days of delivery. Your reviews go from 3 to 5 stars.

Also think about the processing time before shipping. Some suppliers take 1 to 2 business days to prepare, others ship the same day. Start by clearly displaying delivery times on your product page. Your customers prefer an honest deadline to an unpleasant surprise.

FAQS

Is it really free?

No subscription or upfront costs, but you pay for the product + shipping with each order. Some like Modalyst take a 5% commission. The free package available from most providers covers basic functions.

Can you do dropshipping without Shopify?

Yes. WooCommerce and Prestashop dropshipping are free. You can also sell on eBay or Amazon without a website. Shopify remains the simplest thanks to its ecosystem of extensions and dropshipping applications.

What free supplier for France?

  • CJ Dropshipping with European warehouse for the best price-delivery ratio.
  • Syncee to access local European suppliers (fast delivery France).
  • Spocket for verified European suppliers with fast direct delivery.

How much can we win?

Realistic net margin: 15-25% after advertising. On a product sold for €30, count €4-7 in net profit. Choosing the right supplier has a direct impact on your commercial margin. Margins increase when you switch to stock or private label.

Do you need an IOSS number to import from China?

IOSS is an EU VAT scheme for certain distance sales of low-value imported goods. It does not apply to the United Kingdom and does not remove customs duties or the seller's responsibilities. Have your setup checked professionally.

How do you avoid scams?

Order a sample, check Trustpilot reviews, and test customer support before you first order. If the supplier does not display a SIRET code, physical address or legal information, it is a warning signal.

After the supplier, the real work starts!

Dropshipping is an accessible business model. But “free” doesn't mean “effortless.” What will make the difference is your ability to manage customer service, optimize your prices and build a real brand.

Don't get stuck on choosing the supplier. The real work starts afterwards: create an SEO website that converts, test your ads on social networks, improve your offer with customer feedback.

Choose a free supplier from this list of reliable suppliers, import 5 to 10 products, and get started. You will learn more in one week of selling online than in three months of research. Choosing between CJ Dropshipping and AliExpress for your dropshipping store? Compare total cost, sourcing options and estimated delivery for your product.

We screened the platform to give you an honest opinion, based on real user feedback and available public data.

Our verdict on CJ Dropshipping!

CJ Dropshipping is a solid platform for online retailers who want to go further than AliExpress. The free model without a subscription is a real advantage for beginners who are testing products.

The service of sourcing agent staff makes the difference on a daily basis: you have a single contact person who manages your sourcing requests, your order problems and your questions.

On the other hand, the platform is not perfect. The interface is more complex than AliExpress at startup.

Shipping costs vary a lot by product and destination, making calculating margins less predictable. And on some products, unit prices are higher than on AliExpress.

Our score: 7.5/10. A good choice to move from basic dropshipping to a more structured business. Not the magic bullet but an option that inspires confidence if you take the time to calculate your margins well.

If you're also looking for a tool to find winning products and spy on ads that work, Copyfy combines product research, competitive analysis and AI store creation. It complements CJ Dropshipping well in your workflow.

Advantages and disadvantages

What works well

A free plan is available. You can start without a subscription and pay for each product and shipment. CJ also offers optional Plus, Prime and Advanced plans and separately charged services. As with Eprolo, compare the full cost before choosing.

A dedicated personal agent. This is the point that comes up the most in positive reviews. As soon as you sign up, CJ assigns you a customer service agent who can be reached by chat or WhatsApp.

He manages your sourcing, answers your questions and resolves your disputes. Customer support is responsive: several users on Trustpilot mention response times of less than a few hours.

Warehouses in several regions. CJ offers storage and shipping options in China, the US and some European countries. Check the warehouse for each listing: a warehouse in a country does not mean your product is stocked there.

For European customers, stock actually held in the EU can shorten transit and avoid an import at delivery. Confirm stock, timing and fees for each product and destination.

Sourcing on request. Have you spotted a viral product on TikTok but it's not in the CJ catalog? You can post a sourcing request.

You can ask CJ to source a product outside its catalog. Response times depend on the request and supplier availability; confirm the quote before making promises to customers.

Integration with the main platforms. Shopify, WooCommerce, eBay, Wix, Squarespace: the connection is done in a few clicks. The synchronization of orders between your online store and CJ is automatic, which simplifies the management of orders on a daily basis.

What's the problem

Shipping costs are sometimes high. It is the most frequent criticism. A user on CapTERRA reports $60 in shipping for a $60 product. On low tickets (products under €20), shipping costs can eat up your entire margin.

A complex interface at startup. CJ combines the functions of AliExpress and an order management and processing software. In terms of ease of use, that was not its strong point at the beginning. Several users note that the handling is not intuitive the first few days.

Product quality varies. As on any platform that aggregates dropshipping suppliers, the quality is not uniform. Feedback from some users points to products that did not match the photos or poor quality shipments that required customer refunds.

Your products are visible to CJ. The CJ team can see what products you are selling and in what volume.

Concretely, this means that a product that performs well at home could be highlighted on the platform. The risk is low but it exists.

The quality of the agent varies. The personal agent system is an advantage when you come across someone who is responsive. But you don't choose your agent.

Some users report very positive experiences, others report long response times or errors in order processing.

What is CJ Dropshipping exactly?

CJ Dropshipping is a sourcing and order fulfillment platform founded in 2014 in Yiwu, China. This dropshipping supplier offers to act as a link between you (the seller) and Chinese (and international) suppliers. You don't manage inventory or shipping. CJ and its supply chain take care of it.

Concretely, order processing follows three steps:

  1. You list a CJ product in your Shopify or WooCommerce store
  2. A customer places an order on your store
  3. CJ processes the order, packs the product, and ships it directly to the customer

The platform covers categories such as beauty, home, fashion and accessories. Listing counts change; focus on availability of the product you want to sell.

CJ also manages Print on Demand (POD), custom packaging and private labels for those who want to go further in branding.

CJ combines a catalog, sourcing, warehousing and shipping. To assess capacity for your product, check stock, warehouse and carrier options rather than a platform-wide order figure.

How to get started with CJ Dropshipping

Registration is free and takes a few minutes. You create a free account on the cjdropshipping.com website, you link your online store (Shopify, WooCommerce or other) and you start browsing the catalog. Payment for products is made as and when your orders are placed.

Step 1: connect your store. In your CJ dashboard, you authorize the connection with your e-commerce platform. The CJ Shopify app is free and can be downloaded directly from the Shopify App Store.

Step 2: import products You browse the catalog or use the search engine. Once you find a product, you can import it into your store in one click with photos, descriptions and prices. The listing is ready in a few seconds.

Step 3: set up shipping. CJ shows different lines by product and destination. Compare price, tracking and estimated delivery, then include processing time before promising a date.

For US customers, a product already stocked locally may arrive sooner. Actual timing depends on carrier, address and handling.

Step 4: Place a test order. Before you start ads, order the product yourself. Check the quality, the packaging and the actual deadlines.

It is non-negotiable. Without this step, you are taking the risk of selling a product that you have never seen.

A piece of advice : don't limit yourself to the existing catalog. If you've identified a winning product through a tool like Copyfy or the Facebook Ads Library, use the sourcing function to ask CJ to find it from a supplier.

The main functionalities

Free product sourcing

You send a photo, an AliExpress link or even a description and CJ finds you the supplier. The service is included in the free plan with a daily request quota. Premium members have a higher quota and priority treatment.

Print on Demand (POD)

CJ offers a print-on-demand service on customizable T-shirts, mugs, phone cases, and other products. You upload your design, you list the product and CJ prints it with each order. No stock to manage.

Custom packaging

You can add your logo, thank you cards or branded packaging to your orders. This personalization is chargeable (additional costs per order) but it allows you to differentiate your brand from shops that deliver in plastic bags without identity.

Quality control

CJ offers pre-shipment inspections. The team checks that the product corresponds to what was ordered, takes photos and sends them to you for validation.

It is not systematic on all orders but it is available on request.

Product video

An original service: CJ can shoot videos of your products in its studios in China. For creative advertisers, this can be useful if you don't have the resources to produce your own videos at the beginning.

The rates: how much does CJ Dropshipping cost?

CJ’s core plan is free, with no sign-up fee or minimum for a standard order. Optional plans and services are paid: check product, shipping and add-on costs before selling.

You only pay for:

  • The product price (competitive wholesale price, often close to AliExpress rates)
  • Les shipping costs (varies according to weight, destination and carrier chosen)
  • Any storage fees if you hold stock at CJ; check the free period and rates for your warehouse.
  • Les inbound/outbound fees if you send your own products to a European warehouse

The tiered membership system

CJ lists a free plan and paid tiers called Plus, Prime and Advanced. Paid tiers include more sourcing requests and some additional benefits; check their terms before subscribing.

Benefits and quotas vary by plan; check the current terms when choosing.

Plus, Prime and Advanced are optional subscriptions, not levels automatically granted according to spending.

How much does it cost in practice?

Illustrative example: if a product costs €5 and shipping €3–8, product plus shipping costs €8–13. Get an actual quote for your product and destination.

At a €30 selling price, €17–22 remains after product and shipping costs alone. That amount does not prove profitability: advertising, payment fees, returns and taxes still need to be deducted.

In this example, the selling price is 2.31 to 3.75 times product and shipping cost, not four to five times. Calculate net margin after all costs before running ads.

The calculation is complicated on heavier or bulky products, where shipping costs increase quickly. Use the shipping calculator on the CJ site before getting started on a product.

Name: SEO optimization on Shopify to dominate Google!
Introduction: Shopify has everything to perform well in SEO, as long as you know the right settings. The 8 technical and content levers to climb your store up on Google!
Article:
The essential elements:

  • Shopify provides a solid SEO base when you prioritize technical settings, content, architecture and search intent.
  • A common audit point is product URL variants generated through collections, their canonicals and the internal links that create them.
  • The most important optimizations: optimized title tags, lightweight images, architecture, clean URLs, sitemap submitted to Google, and search intent.
  • The 3 important apps: SEO Manager (technical), TinyIMG (images), Judge.me (customer reviews).
  • SEO results vary by site, competition and query: measure early, improve consistently and avoid promises about timing or traffic multiples.

Is Shopify a good choice of CMS in terms of SEO?

Yes, Shopify can provide a good SEO base. Audit URL variants, canonicals, architecture, content and performance before prioritizing fixes.

Shopify's 3 real strengths for SEO :

  1. Speed to market : you can launch an MVP store very quickly
  2. Strong technical infrastructure : ultra-fast hosting, automatic SSL certificate, native responsive
  3. Mature app ecosystem: targeted apps can help, but they do not replace an audit or editorial and technical work

The 2 pitfalls to avoid absolutely :

  1. Believing that Shopify does everything by itself
  2. Install 15 SEO apps and think they'll do the work for you

The 8 essential SEO settings in Shopify

1. Headings and meta descriptions: where to edit them (and how to optimize them)

Go in Online Store > Pages/Products/Collections then click on any page. Scroll down to the “Overview in search engine results” section.

The golden rule :

  • Title: descriptive, distinct and aligned with intent; use the main topic naturally and check how it appears in results
  • Meta description: summarize the page clearly and encourage the click; adapt it to the query instead of a rigid length

Concrete example :

❌ Wrong title: “Product - My store”
✅ Good title: “40L waterproof backpack - 48h delivery”

❌ Bad meta: “Check out our quality backpack.”
✅ Good meta: “Heavy-duty hiking backpack. Waterproof, 40L, 2 year warranty. Free delivery from 50€.”

2. Images: the war against file size

Heavy images can hurt load performance and user experience. Measure real pages before and after optimization instead of assuming an automatic penalty.

Immediate action :

  • Compress all your images before uploading (target: less than 200KB per image)
  • Uses the WEBP format (best quality/weight ratio)
  • Always fill in the ALT text with the description text of your product: “40L waterproof backpack black front view”

3. Navigation and menus, the architecture that boosts your SEO

Your navigation = the map you give to Google to explore your site.

Recommended structure :

  • Main menu: all of your main collections + “about” or “track my order” pages for example
  • Footer menu: links to important pages (CGV, contact, buying guide)
  • Breadcrumb: activate it in your theme settings

Why is it important? Because Google crawls your site by following your internal links. If an important page is only accessible in 5 clicks, it will be poorly referenced. Choose a maximum of 3 clicks from the home page to access any page in your store.

4. Product URLs: the setting we always forget

By default, some Shopify themes generate URLs like: ta-boutique.com/products/product-name-123456

Change immediately the slug into something clean:

  • Remove odd numbers and codes
  • Keep the slug short, descriptive and readable without imposing a fixed word count
  • Include your main keyword

example : ❌ /products/waterproof hiking-backpack-40l-black-ref-12345
✅ /products/waterproof-backpack-40l

Find your next winning product for free !

5. Activate automatic image compression

In Settings > Files, activates automatic image optimization. It compresses your images on the fly with no visible loss of quality.

Measure the actual impact: gains depend on initial weight, theme, apps, network and page. A smaller file does not translate into a fixed speed or ranking gain.

6. Search preference settings

Go in Online store > Preferences and check mark:

  • Do not systematically hide legal pages: they contribute to site legitimacy. Keep them accessible and decide on noindex case by case after an audit
  • “Index the pages of the site” (check that it is activated)

Copyfy tip: Make sure that the pages you want to position on Google are INDEXED, to check enter this command into Google site:urldelapage.fr, if no results come out, index the non-indexed pages via the Search Console or via a third-party tool. No indexing = No ranking.

7. Check your sitemap.xml

Your sitemap is automatically generated by Shopify. Check it out here: ta-shop.com/sitemap.xml

What should appear :

  • All your product pages
  • All your collections
  • Your blog posts
  • Your important static pages

A common issue: “/collections/product-name” URLs (and how to audit them)

By:

{{product.url}}

Why is this model so beneficial?

Before moving on to the steps in this guide, understand why the high ticket dropshipping model attracts just as much. Advertising costs have exploded in recent years. Making a profit on a €20 product has become a losing battle. The cost of customer acquisition often exceeds the margin generated on each sale.

Well-being at home. Infrared saunas, inflatable hot tubs, professional massage equipment. This market is growing by 15% per year. Buyers are investing in their health. Demand remains strong all year round.

Use Google Trends to check for stable demand over 12 months. An upward or flat curve indicates a healthy market. Avoid excessive seasonal peaks that complicate the management of your business.

Forget traditional Asian suppliers for this dropshipping model. Your customers pay €1,500 for a premium item. They expect delivery in 3 to 5 days and impeccable after-sales service. Direct manufacturers. Contact European brands that produce high-end items. Many accept dropshipping partnerships if you present a serious project. They are looking to expand their online sales.

Specialized wholesalers. Each niche has its distributors on the market. For fitness, explore professional sports wholesalers. For premium furniture, contact importers of Scandinavian or Italian brands.

Phone number visible everywhere. It is the strongest signal that you are a serious business. Customers who buy high-end products want to be able to call before confirming their purchase.
